articles.title: República Checa - España, final del Mundial Sub-15 en directo
articles.summary: ¡FINAAAAAAAL DEL PARTIDOOOO! España vence a República Checa (0-3) y es la campeona del primer Mundial Sub-15 de la historia. Un minuto para el final y
articles.body:
Muuuuuuuuuy buenas tardeeeees. Día grande para el fútbol base español, día de los que se recuerdan: España juega la primera final de la historia de la Copa Mundial y Festival Sub-15 de la FIFA . En el Baku Crystal Hall, a partir de las tres de la tarde, la generación de 2011 que esta vez dirige David Gordo se mide a la República Checa con un título inédito en juego y la etiqueta de favorita colgada del cuello. Nueve partidos, nueve victorias y 39 goles después, a la Rojita le queda el último escalón, el más alto, para cerrar un curso redondo en las categorías inferiores.

Enfrente espera el otro invicto del torneo, y no es un rival cualquiera. La República Checa llega también con pleno, con 52 goles a favor y por el camino dos víctimas de campanillas: eliminó a Italia en octavos y tumbó a Brasil en los penaltis de cuartos. Las dos selecciones comparten una cifra que promete igualdad, los nueve goles encajados cada una, pero la diferencian los matices: España reparte el gol entre diez futbolistas distintos, mientras los checos lo concentran en un killer, Ondrej Schwab , con trece dianas y la costumbre de golpear pronto. Gane quien gane, saldrá de Bakú el primer campeón de la historia de esta competición.

articles.title: Cónclave en el fondo con los ultras y fiesta incompleta: La 'Vida Pirata' no sonó en Vallecas
articles.standfirst: Después de la victoria sobre el Celta de Vigo no se cantó el himno de la afición
articles.summary: Después de la victoria sobre el Celta de Vigo no se cantó el himno de la afición
articles.body: Después de la victoria ante el Celta de Vigo, la plantilla del Rayo Vallecano hizo un corro en el césped. Con Beñat San José como la voz cantante felicitó a los jugadores, antes de que todo el equipo agradeciera a la afición el apoyo durante el partido. Cuando se acercaban al fondo de animación y aún quedaba público en las gradas para escuchar la 'Vida Pirata' ocurrió lo contrario. Primero fue Unai López el que se acercó a hablar con un aficionado del fondo de animación y después Isi Palazón. El de Cieza llamó a sus compañeros para que se acercaran al fondo y mantuvieron una conversación. Beñat San José no quiso hablar sobre ese diálogo y por qué no se había cantado la 'Vida Pirata', pero agradeció el gesto. "Agradezco esa conexión también para que nos lo expliquen”, afirmó el técnico vasco. “Nosotros respetamos mucho cuando deciden no animarnos o no celebrar algo de una manera tradicional. Agradecerles la explicación. Considero que a la afición hay que escucharla y hay que progresar en esa comunicación”, afirmó Beñat al ser consultado sobre esa reunión con la afición. Después de la reunión entre representantes de la afición y José María Sardá y Alfonso Martín Presa, desde el fondo se desplegaron pancartas con esas peticiones que se están negociando durante el partido ante el Celta como el precio de los abonos o la estancia del estadio en Vallecas. Se siguen dando acercamientos entre todas las partes, pero la protesta sigue. Por otra parte, el club ha confirmado que los jugadores ya no hablarán en zona mixta. Además, durante los próximos días habrá un portavoz para hablar sobre los temas extra deportivos.

articles.title: Georgia is back to being Georgia, and the rest of college football should be terrified
articles.summary: A Halloween beatdown of Florida should scare the daylights out of anybody who bothered to question Kirby Smart's crew.
articles.body:
ATLANTA — What's it like when Kirby Smart has two weeks after a stunning loss to chew on steel, invent curse words that have never been heard by human ears and soak his team in a marinade of hatred and bile that gets reserved for one particular opponent every year? What happens inside Georgia's football building when a coach with an organic and lifelong distaste for Florida, who savors the opportunity to deliver a good butt-chewing like a fancy bottle of red wine and finally is given a reason to go nuclear on his team after that shocker of a loss to Auburn?

"Honestly, it's just the same," Georgia linebacker Chris Cole said. "Like, if we'd have won that game or if we lost, we were still going back to work. We knew coming into this game we had to get better and better."

Maybe we'll find out otherwise some time before the end of the weekend in one of those leaked fire-and-brimstone speeches that seem to find their way out of the Georgia locker room after every big game. Then again, the Bulldogs left plenty of evidence on the field in a 27-8 thrashing of Florida about what the last couple weeks must have been like in Athens.

As the calendar flips to November, there is little doubt about the national championship favorite. Miami may have come into the weekend as the nation's No. 1 ranked team, but when you see Georgia play like that —Georgia in its full tilt, buttoned-up, grind-you-down glory — who else in this crazy sport are you supposed to bank on?

The Auburn game two Saturdays ago? Yeah, that wasn't the real Georgia. That was an imposter that momentarily conceded to the meat-grinder effect that has turned the SEC into an unpredictable mess where everyone is susceptible to a hangover and nearly anyone can rise up on a given Saturday and put a pelt on the wall.

But this effort against Florida was the genuine article: A defense choking off the point of attack and creating havoc with its size and athleticism, an offense that plays with the lead like an anaconda slowly squeezing the life out of its prey.

As it turned out, Georgia wore an ill-fitting costume two weeks ago against Auburn. On Halloween, the Bulldogs came to the Cocktail Party as themselves.

"We left a lot out there to be desired," Smart said. "We can play a lot better offensively, but we did what we had to do and we avoided turnovers for the most part and we got turnovers. The Dawgs didn't beat the Dawgs today."

What a luxury for a coach to understand that your personnel is so good and your team so balanced that the key in any given game is as simple as not beating yourself. How many other programs can really say that in this era where it seems like everyone has a potentially fatal weakness?

Even though the 19-point margin may not look that impressive on the surface, this one was over quickly and decisively. The entire second half felt like a slog through garbage time, since there was no pathway at all for Florida to make up a 24-0 halftime deficit. It looked as close to vintage Georgia as we've seen in awhile against a quality opponent.

But don't expect Smart to relax — not for even a second. Because not only does Georgia have to get right back up for a key road game next week against Ole Miss, but Smart said something really interesting Saturday night about the overall state of college football.

For some reason, and he can't quite put his finger on it, things feel different this year. Even Georgia, famous for its "Bloody Tuesday" full-pad practices, can't reproduce the level of physicality during the week that propelled Georgia to national titles in 2021 and 2022.

"I've asked several coaches about it and we all have speculation," Smart said. "Everybody's practicing less, but everybody's getting injured more and it doesn't make sense. It doesn't add up."

Is it the 105-man roster limit impacting depth? Are players making so much money now that they want to preserve their bodies in a way that wasn't the case when impressing NFL scouts was crucial to making millions of dollars? Is the spread of talent around the country making it impossible for teams to be consistent from week to week?

"I don't have a good answer for that," Smart said. "People's depth is going to show up and you have to make a choice. How do you want to practice? Do you want to practice at all or do you want to just try to save everybody? It'll be interesting. It's just a different day and age."

In that kind of world, banking on Georgia seems like a good bet. There are rare exceptions — including early exits from the College Football Playoff the last two years — but for the most part you know what you're going to get from Georgia. Even when things aren't perfect, nobody in college football has a higher floor of performance.

Most of the time, like Saturday, the offensive stats don't even really matter. Quarterback Gunner Stockton finished with 101 passing yards on 13 completions against Florida — in other words, he was mostly a non-factor — yet it felt like he could have done a lot more if necessary.

At some point, it will matter. But that's why Georgia is 72-8 since the start of the 2021 season: They rarely need to play their best game to win.

"It might not be perfect, but we can strive to be that," Stockton said.

That's what makes Georgia so scary. Here they are, 7-1 and a near-lock for the CFP after embarrassing their most important historical rival, and they still haven't played a complete football game where everything works the way they expect.

"I don't know when that's going to happen for us," Smart said, "but we can be really good if we're clicking on both sides of the ball."

Trick-or-treat, college football. On Halloween, Georgia got back to being Georgia and showed just how scary it can be simply by being itself.

articles.title: AFC Women's Champions League: East Bengal women seek to scale new summit in Asia
articles.summary: KOLKATA: Armed with hard-won lessons from last season, East Bengal women are on a mission to scale a new continental summit for Indian football.
articles.body: KOLKATA: Armed with hard-won lessons from last season, East Bengal women are on a mission to scale a new continental summit for Indian football. The two-time IWL winners begin their group stage campaign in the AFC Women's Champions League against Vietnamese Ho Chi Minh City WFC here on Sunday.In the last year's campaign held in China's Wuhan, Anthony Andrews' Moshal Girls became the first Indian side to win a match in the group stage of Asia's premier women's club competition but agonizingly stopped short of progressing to the quarterfinals after losing their last match 0-3 to PFC Nasaf of Uzbekistan. Had East Bengal lost that match 0-2, they would have progressed to the knockout stage.Now drawn in Group B, Anthony Andrews' Moshal Girls will also take on South Korea's Hwacheon KSPO WFC on Nov 4 and North Korea's 4.25 SC three days later. In a first for Indian football, East Bengal have been given the honour of hosting the AWCL Group Stage matches and their all three matches at Kishore Bharati Krirangan will kick off at 8pm."Last season's heartbreak helped us understand much better in terms of what the players should do at the bigger level. Obviously the game is faster at the international level and that's how we have strengthened the side this season. We have played a few good tactical games to understand if we can solve problems what we had faced last season," Andrews told reporters during the pre-match news conference at a New Town hotel on Saturday."The girls are ready to put their best foot forward," added the 30-year-old, who is also working with India's U-17 women's team as an assistant coach.The top two from three groups of four teams as well as the two best third-placed sides will advance to the quarterfinals from the 12-team group stage.With a mission to accomplish in Asian football, the red-and-gold management has bolstered the side with the acquisition of India internationals Rimpa Haldar and Thoibisana Chanu as well as Japan's Hitomi Tanaka and Ghanaian trio Olivia Anokye, Adama Alhassan and Abigail Antwi.East Bengal have qualified for the group stage for the second consecutive season after topping Group A in the competition's preliminary stage in Malaysia last Aug in breathtaking style, scoring 18 goals in three games and conceding none.Home is where the team's hopes lie now and midfielder Sathi Debnath is determined to make the most of it."The Kishore Bharati Krirangan has been a bastion of the club and this is the venue where I had got my first trophy with East Bengal women's team (Kanyashree Cup in 2023)," the midfielder said."Because of some momentary lapses, we missed out on the quarterfinal berth by a whisker last season. At home, we'll try to rectify those mistakes (of Wuhan campaign) and reach the knockouts," Debnath said, representing the team's new-look ambitions.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: USC takes down No. 2 Ohio State for its biggest Big Ten win yet
articles.summary: The Buckeyes entered the game without star QB Julian Sayin after his shoulder injury against Indiana.
articles.body:
Lincoln Riley finally has a signature Big Ten victory at USC. And Ohio State's College Football Playoff chances could be in real peril.

The Trojans beat No. 2 Ohio State 30-18 on Saturday night in the Buckeyes' first game without quarterback Julian Sayin, who suffered a potentially season-ending right shoulder injury in OSU's win over No. 4 Indiana on Oct. 17.

Trailing by 11 at halftime, Ohio State had a chance to get back into the game in the third quarter. But Luke Fahey's pass to Isaiah West ended up as a fumble that was recovered by the Trojans after the Buckeyes had gotten into USC territory.

Then USC freshman tight end Max Bowman went to work. The former five-star recruit and No. 44 recruit in the country broke off a 70-yard catch-and-run that included a hurdle and a bunch of broken tackles. Just watch as he sliced through the Ohio State defense like few players have been able to do.

Two plays later, King Miller had given USC an 18-point lead. The game was over from there.

Ohio State cut the lead to nine on a Jeremiah Smith TD catch with 2:12 to go, but the ensuing 2-point conversion failed when Fahey's pass sailed out of the end zone.

We're not going to blame you if you're still skeptical of the Trojans. This is a team that lost 24-7 at Wisconsin a week ago and had negative rushing yards. It's also the same USC team that was dominated by an Oregon team that's had a hard time getting its act together.

But if you want to look on the bright side for USC … the playoff is a very real possibility. After an off week in Week 10, USC has trips against No. 4 Indiana and No. 7 UCLA remaining. If USC wins both of those games — and also beats Maryland — then it's in the playoff. There will be no debate.

USC's offensive stats Saturday night were hardly eye-popping. But that's also because the Trojans barely had the ball. Ohio State held onto the ball for two-thirds of the game and ran double the plays. USC had just 339 yards. But it also ran 49 plays.

The victory is the first over a top-five team in Riley's time in Los Angeles. If you're still pessimistic about USC's playoff chances, you were probably also wondering if Riley would be able to survive a loss on Saturday night to an Ohio State team with a true freshman quarterback making his first career start.

That factor also can cloud the significance of the win. Even though Ohio State was favored by 6.5 points, it's easy to see how this is a game that the Trojans should have won.

And how real are Ohio State's playoff hopes?

Are the Buckeyes a playoff team without Sayin? Saturday night was the example of how they can easily end up missing the postseason without him.

The Buckeyes have Oregon, Northwestern, Nebraska and Michigan remaining in the regular season. Ohio State will be favored in all four of those games, but they're far from guaranteed wins. Especially if the Buckeyes' defense plays the way it did on Saturday night. USC averaged nearly 7 yards a play before kneel downs to drain the final seconds off the clock.

With Fahey at quarterback and the Ohio State run game also missing Ja'Kobi Jackson, the Buckeyes' defense needed to remain elite for Ohio State to continue to be a title contender. Until Saturday night, only Texas — which scored 24 points — had scored more than 19 points against the Buckeyes.

And it wasn't only Bowman breaking big plays, either. WR Trent Mosley scored a 69-yard TD on the second offensive play of the game.

If Ohio State is making the College Football Playoff, it needs to go undefeated in November. And even then, barring a big improvement from what we saw on Saturday night, the Buckeyes are no longer real title contenders.

articles.title: North Carolina recovers two onside kicks, but both are overturned by penalties as No. 1 Miami stays undefeated
articles.summary: The Tar Heels lost their recoveries because of separate offsides and illegal block penalties.
articles.body:
The No. 1 Miami Hurricanes had an upset scare against the University of North Carolina but left Chapel Hill with a 38-35 win.

This game came down to the wire and had one of the wilder endings you will probably ever see.

North Carolina scored a late touchdown and needed to attempt an onside kick, which has an 18% recovery rate across the FBS this season.

The Tar Heels recovered the first, but were whistled for being offsides.

UNC re-kicked the onside kick and recovered it yet again. This one was also called back, but for an illegal block. A block was laid on a Miami player before the ball traveled 10 yards, which is a penalty.

Three attempts were too many, and Miami finally recovered. The Hurricanes tempted fate by running the ball to end the game, only going into victory formation for the final snap, but they didn't suffer a surprise loss as they did a few years ago to Georgia Tech.

Miami scored on its opening drive as Darian Mensah found Malachi Toney for a 2-yard touchdown. The Hurricanes led 17-14 at halftime and 24-21 heading into the fourth quarter.

North Carolina took the 28-24 lead after a 16-play drive that lasted nearly 8:30 and ended with Demon June punching in the 1-yard score at the goal line.

Miami responded with a four-minute drive, and Mark Fletcher Jr. scored his second touchdown of the game. The Hurricanes defense then forced a fumble, which was the lone turnover of the game. On the ensuing possession, Toney caught a 9-yard pass for his second touchdown.

UNC faced an uphill battle, but Billy Edwards Jr. got the Tar Heels downfield and into the end zone in five plays (thanks to two Miami penalties for a combined 25 yards).

Down three, North Carolina kept giving its fans hope with not one, but two onside-kick recoveries, both overturned by two close penalties.

Miami remains undefeated at 8-0 and will surely remain No. 1 as the Hurricanes face No. 5 Notre Dame next week.

North Carolina's loss drops the Tar Heels to 4-4, including a 2-3 mark in ACC games. UNC is now 0-12 all-time against the AP's No. 1-ranked team.

articles.title: College football winners and losers: How we think the initial College Football Playoff rankings will look after Week 9
articles.summary: What will the top 12 look like on Tuesday night?
articles.body:
It's time to start seriously discussing the College Football Playoff .

The arrival of November means the College Football Playoff selection committee's rankings are here. Tuesday night, we'll get the first set of CFP rankings and an initial chance to see what the committee is thinking.

That thinking will seemingly change from week to week. Consistency can be hard to come by. But given our years of seeing how the CFP has evaluated teams in the four and now 12-team playoff formats, here's our best guess at how the rankings will look on Nov. 3.

Highest Group of Six team: Boise State (6-1)

With James Madison's two-game losing streak and a morass of teams in the American Conference, the Broncos look poised to get their second CFP berth in three years. Boise's biggest challenger looks like Oregon State at the moment. But November could bring a surprise or two.

Ole Miss fans shouldn't be worried where the team is in Tuesday night's rankings. Next week's game against Georgia will quickly render it irrelevant. The Rebels are in the playoff with a 4-0 finish to the season and could even sneak in at 9-3 overall if things break their way.

The Longhorns are ahead of Ole Miss thanks to that head-to-head win, and that win over Ohio State still holds weight. Games at Missouri and LSU over the next two weeks will be huge for the Longhorns' hopes. They might be able to afford a single loss over the rest of the season. But this is a team that was 9-3 and missed the College Football Playoff a year ago.

Kentucky's résumé is a great litmus test. There's no doubt that the Wildcats have been one of the best teams in the SEC this season. But just how do you view Kentucky's schedule? Wins over Oklahoma and Texas A&M aren't nearly as impressive as they once looked and that Alabama loss was a blowout. But like Ole Miss fans, Kentucky fans shouldn't get worked up at where the Wildcats are on Tuesday night. Games against Tennessee, Florida and Missouri will sort things out over the course of November.

Are the Buckeyes real title contenders at this point? We're not so sure. It was always going to be a tough ask with a freshman quarterback making his first career start at USC, but the Ohio State defense gave up nearly 7 yards a play to a USC team that had minus-17 rushing yards a week ago. Can this version of Ohio State go 4-0 in November against Northwestern, Oregon, Nebraska and Michigan?

We think the Tide will be ahead of Kentucky because of that head-to-head win and it helps that the Tide's two losses are to two teams in the top 20 of the AP poll. It wouldn't be a shock if Alabama was behind the Wildcats and at No. 10 on Tuesday night, but a win over LSU in Week 10 will go a long way toward showing how good this team actually is.

Two things can be true at the same time: The turnaround that Bob Chesney is engineering at UCLA is probably the best coaching job in the country. And it's also hard to take this team seriously as a national title contender, especially with QB Nico Iamaleava sidelined for the rest of the season. UCLA's best wins are over Wisconsin and Oregon. Both are struggling and the Ducks turned the ball over seven times in the Bruins' two-point win. We think the committee is going to significantly ding UCLA's strength of schedule given the way it's previously evaluated top-tier teams.

The head-to-head principle applies here. It's hard to put Notre Dame ahead of BYU since the Cougars beat the Irish even if Notre Dame should have received one last shot at the end zone. The Irish overpowered Navy in the second half on Saturday and will be much closer to No. 1 with a win over Miami in Week 10.

The Cougars did what they needed to do in a win over Arizona State on Saturday ahead of a massive game against Utah. Can you tell Week 10 is going to be really, really good? BYU is at risk of missing the Big 12 title game with a loss to the Utes, however. Texas Tech is lurking with a manageable schedule. The Red Raiders aren't as good as they were a season ago, but avoid both BYU and Utah in Big 12 play.

The Hoosiers' offense has been a rough watch recently. Indiana hasn't scored more than 20 points in each of its last four games and Curt Cignetti switched quarterbacks at halftime of its overtime win over Minnesota after Josh Hoover took a big hit at the end of the first half. Hoover doesn't look 100% since he appeared to get injured in the second half against Ohio State. How will the committee factor that in? This is still a team with an elite defense, though the special teams are looking very shaky.

Utah appears to be a more complete team than Indiana at this point, and we think the lack of a loss puts the Utes ahead of the Hoosiers. Saturday's trip to Cincinnati had all the makings of a trap after a big win over Houston and the Holy War looming. Instead, Utah made easy work of the Bearcats in a 49-25 win.

The Bulldogs ended their rivalry game with Florida before halftime. The Gators were overwhelmed by Georgia in the first half as it was clear that the Bulldogs are the best team in the SEC despite that blip against Auburn two weeks ago. Had Georgia beaten Auburn, we think the Bulldogs would be No. 1 Tuesday night.

The Hurricanes have two of the top three Heisman favorites in the country in QB Darian Mensah and WR Malachi Toney and an offense that looks to be the best in the country. The Hurricanes got a scare from North Carolina on Saturday, but Mensah threw for 274 yards and three scores while Toney caught two of them and Mark Fletcher rushed for two more. Who else can't wait for next Saturday night and the Hurricanes' trip to Notre Dame?

Here are the rest of this week's winners and losers.

Sacramento State : The Hornets got their first win over an FBS team as an FBS team in a 31-10 win over Kent State on Friday night. Sac State made the jump to the top level of college football in the offseason and joined the MAC. The conference affiliation has led to a lot of cross-country travel for both the Hornets and their midwestern opponents. Friday night, Isaiah Ene rushed for 107 yards and two TDs on 19 carries as the Sacramento State defense forced five turnovers.

Oregon: Given the way the 2026 season has gone, you could understand if Oregon folded after No. 20 Northwestern took a 20-6 lead with less than two minutes to go in the first half. Instead, the Ducks outscored the Wildcats 21-6 in the second half on the way to a 34-26 win. Dylan Raiola had his best game of the season as he was 22-of-31 passing for 336 yards and three touchdowns, and RB Brandon Smith rushed eight times for 82 yards and a score.

Clemson: The Tigers went into Tallahassee and put Florida State further into its feelings with a 36-24 win. Tait Reynolds threw two touchdown passes and ran for another as he had the best game of his young career. Entering Saturday night, Reynolds had thrown just one TD all season. The Clemson defense held FSU to 65 rushing yards and forced four turnovers thanks to three Ashton Daniels interceptions.

Utah: The No. 6 Utes made sure that Cincinnati was not going to knock off an undefeated team for the second straight week. Utah scored 42 first-half points in a 49-25 demolition of the Bearcats. Devon Dampier threw three touchdowns and Utah rushed for 268 yards on just 42 carries. The Utes scored TDs on each of their four offensive possessions of the first half, Rabbit Evans returned a fumble for 51 yards and a TD, and Elijah Davis had a 39-yard pick-6 before the game was even at halftime.

James Madison: The Dukes have now lost back-to-back games in overtime after a 7-0 start. James Madison fell 24-21 at home to Troy on Thursday night thanks to five turnovers and a costly decision to not kick a field goal in overtime.

Justin Powe intercepted JMU QBs Camden Coleman and JC Evans three times, and receivers Michael Scott and Jeremiah Harrison each fumbled. JMU still had a chance to win the game in regulation, but its drive as the fourth quarter expired ended at the Troy 37-yard line.

In overtime, Billy Napier chose to go for it on fourth-and-1 at the Troy 5-yard line, but Seth Cromwell got stuffed. From there, Troy only needed a field goal for the win.

Nebraska: The Huskers have now lost three straight games after a 17-10 defeat at home to Washington. Is it a coincidence that the three-game losing streak to Indiana, Oregon and now Washington comes after the first five wins of the season were against Ohio, Bowling Green, North Dakota, Michigan State and Maryland? We'll let you decide on that one. The Huskers travel to Illinois on Friday night and then to Rutgers before games against Ohio State and Iowa. An 8-4 season is still on the table.

Oklahoma: The Sooners cannot string two wins together. OU has now alternated wins and losses through its first eight games of the season after a 42-25 home loss to a resurgent South Carolina team. The Oklahoma defense has been one of the best in the country and had three interceptions. Yet South Carolina had over 500 yards of total offense as LaNorris Sellers threw for 301 yards on just 24 pass attempts while John Mateer had just 244 on 43 throws.

Sam Houston: The Bearkats are in the market for a new head coach after a 24-3 loss to Missouri State on Tuesday. The loss dropped Sam Houston to 1-7 overall and 0-4 in Conference USA. And on Wednesday, Phil Longo was fired. Longo won just three games since he was hired ahead of the 2025 season to replace KC Keeler. Eric Raisbeck and Freddie Aughtry-Lindsay will serve as the co-interim coaches for the rest of the season as Sam Houston learns that going from FCS powerhouse to competitive Group of Six team is a pretty tall task.

articles.title: Yahoo Top 10: Ohio State tumbles out of rankings, paving way for a new No. 1
articles.summary: USC's big win over the Buckeyes shook up the top of the rankings.
articles.body:
USC put Ohio State in danger of falling out of the College Football Playoff picture before November even arrived — and it pushed the Buckeyes out of the Top 10, too.

The Trojans downed the Buckeyes in the LA Coliseum in what many thought could be Riley's swan song. Ohio State couldn't slow down quarterback Jayden Maiava and receiver Trent Mosley and the Trojans enough on Saturday night in a 30-18 victory .

Ryan Day's team slipped out of our rankings and Miami became our new No. 1 after the Hurricanes survived a thriller in Chapel Hill .

Meanwhile, Texas Tech outlasted Arizona in the Big 12's big game on Saturday; Indiana and BYU — both in our top 10 — barely won; and Georgia blew out Florida in the SEC.

But Ohio State's loss is a resounding one throughout the sport as quarterback Luke Fahey replaced the injured Julian Sayin. Matt Patricia's defense didn't show up and the Trojans walked away big winners.

The Hurricanes needed a sack-fumble and then a touchdown from, of course, Malachi Toney to secure the victory in a tight game. The Tar Heels led midway through the fourth quarter before Miami's nine-play, 75-yard touchdown drive and then the big turnover that led to Toney's score — his second touchdown of the day.

It took a 60-yard game-tying field goal, a backup quarterback and two clutch catches from receiver Charlie Becker for the Hoosiers to survive a scare at home from the Gophers. Reserve QB Grant Wilson — a seventh-year senior! — entered for injured Josh Hoover to pass for 156 yards. He hit Becker for two of his nine completions on the field goal drive to push it to overtime and on the eventual game-winner in the extra period.

The Bruins didn't need much from QB Ty Dieffenbach considering their resounding defensive performance. The Wolf Pack had 176 yards of total offense. In the last five games, no team has cracked the 15-point mark against coordinator Colin Hitschler's defense. His group is now allowing less than 270 yards a game. That's a recipe for a playoff berth.

If you worried about the Bulldogs after their loss to Auburn, don't worry any longer. Kirby Smart's team showed why it just might be the SEC's best chance to end the league's three-year skid in the national championship race . QB Gunner Stockton rebounded from that turnover-plagued outing against Auburn two weeks ago by carving through the Gators in Atlanta.

Coach Will Stein and the Wildcats get a much-needed week off before one of the biggest games in school history in Knoxville. This game seems like a loser-is-out-of-the-playoff matchup. QB Kenny Minchey against UT's salty defense is the matchup to watch. He hasn't thrown an interception since the loss to Alabama in Week 2.

QB Devon Dampier had another electric day on the ground and through the air, accounting for more than 300 yards and three passing touchdowns as the Utes extended the nation's long win streak at a whopping 14 games. That's the longest streak since Utah won 16 consecutive games from 2007-2009.

The Irish involved Jerome Bettis Jr. more in the offense on Saturday and that paid off. The son of the Hall of Fame running back caught six passes for 78 yards and finished off the scoring with a 31-yard touchdown catch from CJ Carr. Notre Dame led by just one point, 14-13, at halftime before roaring to life in a second half that included a 23-yard score from Nolan James Jr.

Entering the fourth quarter all tied up, the Cougars needed nine-play and 11-play scoring drives to break the 17-all score and rebound from last week's stunning loss at UCF. BYU managed just 47 yards rushing but QB Bear Bachmeier threw for 236 yards and found six different receivers.

Perhaps the hottest power conference coach this cycle got another big win. Jake Dickert, in Year 2 in Winston-Salem, has the Demon Deacons 7-1 and barreling toward and ACC championship game appearance. Former UNC QB Gio Lopez threw for 229 and ran for 64 in the beatdown of the Cavaliers.

The debate over Arch Manning will continue onward, but there's no argument about whether the Texas defense is good or not. The Longhorns suffocated Mississippi State, winning a second consecutive game after dropping two in a stunning slide that sent them tumbling out of our Top 10. Welcome back, Horns!

articles.title: B/R's 2026 College Football Experts Top 25 Rankings After Week 9
articles.summary: The biggest surprise of the Week 9 college football slate was USC knocking off Ohio State, but the weekend was almost significantly more chaotic.
articles.body:
The biggest surprise of the Week 9 college football slate was USC knocking off Ohio State, but the weekend was almost significantly more chaotic.

Miami, Indiana and BYU all avoided suffering their own upset losses, escaping with narrow victories, and in the case of the Hoosiers needing overtime to do it.

As more teams on the fringe of the Top 25 rankings add a second and third loss to their resume, the door has opened for one-loss Group of Six contenders UTSA and New Mexico to enter the conversation.

Ahead is an updated look at how the college football experts here at B/R line up the nation's top 25 teams following Week 9 action.

Week 9 Result: WIN at San Jose State (21-16) Next Week: at Nevada

The Lobos' only loss this season was a 14-6 game against Oklahoma in Week 3, and their stingy defense has yet to allow 20 points to an opponent this season while going undefeated in Mountain West play. They overcame three interceptions by Toa Fa'avae with a strong running game, led by Kiefer Sibley (12 carries, 102 yards) and Scottre Humphrey (16 carries, 87 yards, 2 TD). A road game against Wyoming on Nov. 21 is their toughest remaining game.

Week 9 Result: BYE Next Week: at Florida Atlantic

The Roadrunners' only loss this season was a Week 3 non-conference game against Texas, and while they are still chasing Boise State in the Group of Six picture, they sit alongside New Mexico as the potential next team up for a playoff bid if the Broncos falter. Veteran quarterback Owen McCown gives them stability under center, while the rushing attack is averaging 184.9 yards per game. The defense will have its hands full slowing down Florida Atlantic quarterback Caden Veltkamp in Week 10.

23. South Carolina (5-3, Previous Rank: NR)

Week 9 Result: WIN at Oklahoma (42-25) Next Week: vs. Texas A&M

After an 0-3 start to SEC play, the Gamecocks have beaten Florida, Tennessee and Oklahoma to climb back into the national picture. LaNorris Sellers had 301 passing yards, 96 rushing yards and five total touchdowns. It was a dominant win for South Carolina, despite three turnovers and nine penalties for 90 yards, proving they can beat a quality conference foe on the road even without playing their best all-around game.

Week 9 Result: WIN at Arkansas (34-10) Next Week: vs. Texas

The Tigers are now 3-2 in conference play with both of those losses coming on the road against Mississippi State and Ole Miss, and as the list of three-loss SEC teams continues to grow, they have leapfrogged several teams in the national picture. Austin Simmons (20/31, 179 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT) and Jamal Roberts (23 carries, 138 yards, 1 TD) led the way offensively, while the Missouri defense came up with four takeaways.

Week 9 Result: LOSS at Texas Tech (26-34) Next Week: vs. TCU

The Wildcats led 23-17 late in the third quarter, but allowed 17 unanswered points and ran out of time on their comeback attempt, taking a second loss that pushes their Big 12 championship and College Football Playoff outlook into longshot territory. Noah Fifita threw for 417 yards, but the Arizona running game was completely neutralized with just 12 rushing yards, and that turned them into a one-dimensional attack down the stretch.

Week 9 Result: WIN vs. Wisconsin (30-0) Next Week: at Northwestern

The Wisconsin defense shutting down USC's offense in a 24-7 victory was one of the biggest stories in college football a week ago, but the Badgers were on the wrong end of a dominant defensive performance on Saturday. The Hawkeyes bounced back from their Week 8 loss to Minnesota by surrendering just nine first downs and 235 total yards while pitching a shutout, logging three takeaways and giving up just 2.2 yards per carry. Quarterback Hank Brown (20/24, 222 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT) had his best game of the season under center.

Week 9 Result: BYE Next Week: vs. Cincinnati

Conner Weigman ranks in the top 10 nationally in total yards (2,302, 10th) and total touchdowns (26, 3rd), and he has the Cougars eyeing a second straight 10-win season. Next week's matchup against Cincinnati stands as their toughest remaining game, and even with losses to Texas Tech and Utah, finishing with a 10-2 record might be enough to keep them alive in the College Football Playoff conversation as the list of three-loss SEC teams continues to grow.

Week 9 Result: WIN vs. Ohio State (30-18) Next Week: BYE

The Trojans set the tone with a pair of first quarter touchdowns, and the defense bent but didn't break in allowing 464 yards of offense but only one touchdown. It was a terrific bounce-back performance for USC following last week's offensive dud against Wisconsin. Jayden Maiava (15/22, 222 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT) and Trent Mosley (5 catches, 101 yards, 1 TD) led the way offensively, and now they have two weeks to prepare for a huge Week 11 matchup with Indiana.

17. Boise State (7-1, Previous Rank: 17)

Week 9 Result: WIN vs. Texas State (46-45) Next Week: at Colorado State

The Broncos trailed 39-28 with 7:50 remaining in the fourth quarter when starting quarterback Maddux Madsen was sidelined with a knee injury. Backup Max Cutforth took the reins for a chaotic finish, throwing for 131 yards on 13 pass attempts and completing three straight drives with touchdown passes. With that, Boise State remains atop the Group of Six picture, as a second loss would have dropped them below teams like UTSA and New Mexico.

16. Wake Forest (7-1, Previous Rank: 16)

Week 9 Result: WIN vs. Virginia (51-7) Next Week: vs. Merrimack

Fresh off a bye week, the Wake Forest offense rolled to 538 total yards while putting points on the board in each of their first nine offensive possessions. Gio Lopez had 229 passing yards and a touchdown, while Ty Clark III tallied three rushing scores to lead a running game that finished with 309 yards and five scores. There is a very real path to an 11-1 finish for this team, starting with a cupcake next weekend.

Week 9 Result: WIN vs. Auburn (45-15) Next Week: vs. Georgia

The Ole Miss defense contained Auburn quarterback Byrum Brown (195 passing yards, 5 rushing yards, 2 TD), came up with two turnovers and held the Tigers to 2.3 yards per carry, and that was more than enough to support a high-powered offense. Trinidad Chambliss had 263 passing yards and two touchdowns to go along with a rushing score, and the Rebels converted 13-of-16 on third down to help rebound in decisive fashion following last week's road loss at Texas.

Week 9 Result: WIN vs. Arizona (34-26) Next Week: vs. West Virginia

Quarterback Thomas Castellanos had 144 passing yards, 117 rushing yards and three total touchdowns in his first start for Texas Tech after Will Hammond was benched following last week's loss to Cincinnati. J'Koby Williams (14 carries, 175 yards, 1 TD) also had a big day on the ground, and the Red Raiders finished with a staggering 328-12 advantage in rushing yardage. They are still chasing Utah and BYU in the Big 12 standings, but a one-loss Texas Tech team would still have a playoff case even if they miss the Big 12 championship game.

Week 9 Result: LOSS at USC (18-30) Next Week: vs. Oregon

The Ohio State offense failed to consistently move the ball with true freshman Luke Fahey (21/38, 260 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT) under center in place of the injured Julian Sayin, and the Buckeyes didn't score a touchdown until there was 2:12 remaining in the fourth quarter. Star wide receiver Jeremiah Smith (10 catches, 83 yards, 1 TD) was held in check, and the Buckeyes will need to find some answers over the final four games to avoid a potentially catastrophic third loss.

Week 9 Result: WIN vs. Mississippi State (31-3) Next Week: at Missouri

An efficient game from Arch Manning (16/20, 220 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT) and a defense that allowed just 2.8 yards per play led the way for the Longhorns in a dominant win, as they improved to 3-2 in SEC play and now have back-to-back victories. The Mississippi State offense had 10 empty possessions with seven punts, one turnover on downs, one missed field goal and one interception, as they struggled to move the ball with Kamario Taylor again watching from the sidelines.

The Crimson Tide rebounded from back-to-back losses with a Week 8 victory over Texas A&M, and Keelon Russell bounced back from a couple shaky individual performances with 311 passing yards and three touchdowns. The Week 10 showdown with LSU could end up being an elimination game in the College Football Playoff picture, and if Alabama can come away with a victory, they will close out the year favored in their final three games against Vanderbilt, Chattanooga and Auburn.

Week 9 Result: BYE Next Week: vs. Kentucky

Quarterback play is the big question mark for the Volunteers. True freshman Faizon Brandon is dealing with injuries and was benched for George MacIntyre, who has been used more as a game manager while the offense leans heavily on DeSean Bishop (171 carries, 957 yards, 11 TD). Their Week 8 loss to South Carolina gives them very little wiggle room going forward if they are going to make the College Football Playoff field, and they still have home games against Kentucky and LSU on the horizon.

Week 9 Result: BYE Next Week: vs. Alabama

With 742 total yards and eight touchdowns the last two weeks in victories over Mississippi State and Auburn, Sam Leavitt has hit his stride after a shaky start to his LSU tenure. He leads the SEC in total yards (2,497) and total touchdowns (25), and he will be the X-factor in the Tigers' push to avoid a third loss as they face off against Alabama, Texas and Tennessee coming out of their bye week. Despite their two losses, they have outscored the opposition by a staggering 321-128 margin on the year.

Week 9 Result: BYE Next Week: at Tennessee

The Wildcats are off to their best start since 2018, and with a 5-1 record in SEC play, they entered Week 9 perched atop the conference standings. They control their own destiny in what has been a surprise season, but the road ahead is tough, as they face Tennessee, Florida and Missouri coming out of their bye week. Notre Dame transfer Kenny Minchey (69.0 cmp%, 1,755 yards, 14 TD, 1 INT) has been a revelation at quarterback.

Week 9 Result: WIN at Navy (35-13) Next Week: vs. Miami

Navy's triple-option offense entered Saturday's game averaging 307.7 rushing yards per game, but they were limited to 48 carries for 212 yards and one touchdown, effectively corralling their offensive attack. The Fighting Irish led just 14-13 at halftime before scoring 21 unanswered points during the second half, and a prime trap game was successfully navigated with a huge showdown against Miami now on the horizon next weekend. CJ Carr (19/29, 210 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT) and Nolan James Jr. (9 carries, 107 yards, 2 TD) were the standouts offensively.

Week 9 Result: WIN at Arizona State (27-20) Next Week: at Utah

A week after suffering their first loss of the season to UCF, the Cougars narrowly avoided disaster, kicking a go-ahead field goal early in the fourth quarter before sealing the victory with an 11-play, 95-yard drive that chewed six minutes off the clock. The BYU rushing attack was non-existent, finishing with 47 yards on 30 carries, and Bear Bachmeier (19/30, 236 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT) did just enough through the air. Next week's showdown with Utah is on track to be the first time in the history of the Holy War both teams were ranked inside the top 10.

Week 9 Result: WIN vs. Nevada (27-0) Next Week: at Minnesota

The Bruins had their first shutout at the Rose Bowl since 2007 in a game where they were 22.5-point favorites, holding Nevada to 176 total yards and 1.9 yards per carry while coming up with four interceptions.

The defense did most of the work, including a first quarter touchdown, and Ty Dieffenbach played a clean game under center with 186 total yards and two scores.

With no Indiana or Ohio State on the schedule, they don't play a ranked opponent the rest of the way.

4. Indiana Hoosiers (8-1, Previous Rank: 4)

Week 9 Result: WIN vs. Minnesota (23-16, OT) Next Week: BYE

Starting quarterback Josh Hoover was benched at halftime as the Hoosiers trailed 10-7, and backup Grant Wilson (9/17, 156 yards, 1 TD, 0 INT, 26 rush yards) threw the go-ahead touchdown pass to Charlie Becker on the first play of overtime.

The Hoosiers offense has averaged just 17.8 points over the past four games, and it took a 60-yard field goal from Paddy McAteer as time expired in regulation to force overtime. That came after Minnesota kicker Luke Drzewiecki drilled his own 60-yarder just 19 seconds earlier.

It might not be the same dominant Indiana squad we saw a year ago, but they have USC, Washington and Purdue after next week's bye, putting them in prime position to return to the College Football Playoff and the Big Ten championship game.

Week 9 Result: WIN at Cincinnati (49-25) Next Week: vs. BYU

After a hard-fought victory over Houston last weekend to remain undefeated, the Utes steamrolled their way to a 42-6 halftime lead and cruised the rest of the way to improve to 8-0 for the first time since 2010.

The first half featured four touchdown drives and two defensive scores in an utterly dominant performance on both sides of the football, and they pounded out 42 carries for 268 yards to dominate time of possession by more than 10 minutes and bring home the win.

With a victory over BYU next weekend, the Utes will have a legitimate case for the No. 1 spot in the Top 25 poll.

2. Georgia Bulldogs (7-1, Previous Rank: 3)

Week 9 Result: WIN vs. Florida (27-8) Next Week: at Ole Miss

The Bulldogs had four takeaways, including a 66-yard fumble return touchdown by Chris Cole, and that was too big of a hole for Florida to overcome. That helped cover up an inconsistent day from the Georgia offense.

Gunner Stockton had just 101 passing yards, 45 rushing yards and zero touchdowns, and the Bulldogs averaged a middling 4.8 yards per play. Nate Frazier and Bo Walker each had a rushing touchdown to cap off long drives.

It wasn't the most well-rounded victory, but it was still a relatively easy win to help keep Georgia tied atop the SEC standings with an idle Kentucky team.

1. Miami Hurricanes (8-0, Previous Rank: 1)

Week 9 Result: WIN at North Carolina (38-35) Next Week: at Notre Dame

North Carolina quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. (28/34, 341 yards, 4 TD, 0 INT) outplayed Darian Mensah (22/29, 274 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT) and the Hurricanes trailed 28-24 early in the fourth quarter, but they managed to pull out the victory with a clutch fourth quarter.

The Miami offense ripped off back-to-back touchdown drives, sandwiched around the only turnover of the game when Marquise Lightfoot knocked the ball loose on one of his two sacks of Edwards.

Mark Fletcher Jr. (13 carries, 43 yards, 2 TD) and Malachi Toney (7 catches, 75 yards, 2 TD) still managed to find the end zone twice each, despite less gaudy yardage totals than usual, and Miami avoided the trap game loss with Notre Dame on the schedule next weekend.

articles.title: Big 12 admits that it incorrectly gave No. 8 BYU a first-quarter touchdown in win over Arizona State
articles.summary: BYU was allowed to advance a fumble by Bear Bachmeier on a QB sneak near the goal line.
articles.body:
The Big 12 has admitted to another officiating error involving BYU.

The conference said Saturday night that it should not have given BYU a touchdown in the first quarter of the No. 8 Cougars' 27-20 win over Arizona State on Saturday.

Running back Sione Moa was credited with a fumble recovery touchdown after quarterback

Bear Bachmeier lost the ball on a QB sneak attempt near the goal line. However, replay officials should have put the ball back to the spot of the fumble for BYU to run a play on third down.

"At 11:27 in the first period of the Arizona State-BYU game, Big 12 replay officials stopped the game to review possession by BYU," the conference said in a statement. "The play showed that the runner lost possession of the ball prior to the forward progress spot, and the ball was recovered by another BYU player at the two-yard line and he was awarded a touchdown. "Rule 12-3-3-d-2 states 'If the replay official rules that the ball was not dead, it belongs to the recovering team at the spot of the recovery and any advance is nullified.' "Replay was incorrect in awarding a score. The correct ruling should have been BYU ball for a third-and-goal attempted from the two-yard line."

"At 11:27 in the first period of the Arizona State-BYU game, Big 12 replay officials stopped the game to review possession by BYU," the conference said in a statement. "The play showed that the runner lost possession of the ball prior to the forward progress spot, and the ball was recovered by another BYU player at the two-yard line and he was awarded a touchdown.

"Rule 12-3-3-d-2 states 'If the replay official rules that the ball was not dead, it belongs to the recovering team at the spot of the recovery and any advance is nullified.'

"Replay was incorrect in awarding a score. The correct ruling should have been BYU ball for a third-and-goal attempted from the two-yard line."

The touchdown was Moa's first of two on the day. He finished with eight carries for 20 yards, while Bachmeier threw for 236 yards and a TD.

Two weeks ago, Big 12 officials failed to give Notre Dame another play at the end of the Fighting Irish's loss to the Cougars. As Notre Dame threw into the end zone while trailing 28-24, CJ Carr's pass fell incomplete with one second remaining on the clock. However, officials failed to review the time remaining on the clock — while also potentially missing a pass interference penalty — and the game ended.

A week ago, UCF upset BYU 39-31 in two overtimes after UCF's potential game-winning kick on third down at the end of the third quarter was blocked. Kicker Will Stone recovered the kick and had his helmet ripped off as he went down with four seconds to go. Officials said that a 10-second runoff was necessary because Stone's helmet came off. However, the clock stops at the end of a blocked kick recovery. And that clock stoppage supersedes a runoff.

Had the clock rules been properly applied, UCF would have gotten another chance to kick a game-winning field goal in regulation.

articles.title: Wales in fight to retain rising female football stars
articles.summary: Wales face an "increasingly aggressive" battle to secure the international futures of talented youngsters tempted to switch to England.
articles.body:
Wales are facing a fight to hold on to some of their most promising female footballers amid an "increasingly aggressive" battle to secure the international futures of talented youngsters.

Wales have already lost rising Manchester United star Layla Drury, the Wrexham-born forward who became the Red Devils' youngest ever female goalscorer in January.

Drury, 17, switched allegiances to England earlier this year having previously represented Wales at under-17 level.

The loss of Drury, who has already played eight times for United's first team, was a heavy blow for Wales given her potential and the fact that she was part of the Football Association of Wales' (FAW) development system.

The concern for the FAW is that further young Welsh talents could be tempted to switch allegiances, with the pull of a potential Lionesses career regarded as significant.

"The market for capturing and retaining talent has become increasingly aggressive," FAW chief football officer David Adams told BBC Sport Wales.

"We must make every effort to protect our assets and retain our top talent to protect the future success of the women's national teams."

Since 2020, the FAW has focused attempts to develop young female players - aged between 11 and 16 - on programmes in north and south Wales.

As part of the system, a group of 31 players are involved in three training sessions a week and play games in the FAW's National Academi boys' set-up in order to aid their development.

There is a further pool of 50 players who compete in Adran Premier academies and train with the FAW's girls' development set-up twice a week, while Wales-qualified girls at English academies are invited to a school holiday regional programme.

The FAW's development programme, which has been awarded Fifa academy status, also focuses on analysis work and strength and conditioning in an attempt to produce future Wales internationals.

A high proportion of players involved are either dual-qualified or have multi-national heritage.

The fact that many of those players are likely to sign for clubs in England when aged 15 to 16 – with no top-class women's clubs to join in Wales – can be problematic for the FAW.

If players are representing English clubs, they are more likely to come to the attention of those working in England's international pathway.

The opportunity to play for England is viewed as appealing for some players because they are one of the women's game's heavyweight sides, having won the Women's Euros twice in a row and reached the Women's World Cup final in 2023.

Fishlock out to keep career alive in NWSL play-offs

Wales under-23s gather for inaugural women’s camp

FAW sets ambitious 10-year plan but seeks more money

As well as the increased chance of success on the pitch, playing for the Lionesses can bring significant commercial opportunities for individual players.

Unlike the men's game, where the biggest financial rewards are on offer at club level, the commercial side of playing international football can be a significant pull for some female players because of the far lower salaries paid at women's clubs.

Former captain Kath Morgan won 51 caps during a 14-year Wales career and has also coached the national side.

She currently coaches Welsh youngsters at Coleg y Cymoedd's full-time female academy and also works as an agent for some players, including new Wales cap Casi Gregson.

Morgan believes young players are driven primarily by a desire to become professionals – and will go wherever it takes to make that happen.

"I don't think it's a decision based on finances - I think it's more based on the chance to have success in their careers," Morgan said.

While there is an acceptance that competing with England's resources is not possible, Morgan argues there is a need for further investment in girls' football in Wales.

"There has to be consistency in creating the pathway," she added.

"The crux of it is that if there's a lack of infrastructure and investment, players will inevitably go to where that is offered."

A hope that players feel 'sense of belonging'

Manchester City centre-back Mayzee Davies, 20, 19-year-old Manchester United full-back Scarlett Hill and United attacking midfielder Mared Griffiths, also 19, have all broken into Rhian Wilkinson's Wales side having been part of the FAW's development system.

Had Drury opted for Wales, the likelihood is that she would also have at least one senior Welsh cap to her name by now, particularly after injuries forced Wilkinson to turn to a number of youngsters for last month's Women's World Cup semi-final games against Albania.

In truth, Drury – like club colleague Griffiths - might already be an international regular had she stuck with Wales.

Instead, she will hope an England senior chance comes at some point in the future having been a late addition to their U20 Women's World Cup squad in September.

Unless there is a change in Fifa regulations, there is no chance of Drury playing for Wales further down the line even if she does not become a Lioness.

The rules state that if a player features in a competitive game for one country – as Drury did for Wales Under-17s – they are allowed only one switch of nationality.

Vera Jones is another highly regarded Welsh-born teenager who is playing for England, though her situation is different.

The attacking midfielder, 18, spent five years in Barry Town's academy before joining Chelsea in 2024.

Currently on loan at Watford, Jones made her England Under-17 debut in 2023 and has remained part of the English set-up, featuring alongside Drury in the U20 Women's World Cup squad.

The difference in Jones' case is that she did not play for Wales before committing to England.

As a result she would – potentially - be eligible to switch to the land of her birth if she does not go on to play senior football for the Lionesses.

Pressure on Norway in play-off final - Wilkinson

Why play-off win may not send Wales to World Cup

Whether that ever becomes a conversation depends on Jones' progress in the English system – as well as her wishes, of course - but Wales are sure to monitor the situation knowing she could one day follow the likes of Hannah Cain and Lois Joel by playing senior football for them having represented England at youth level.

In the meantime, Welsh football's bosses must do all they can to try to ensure the various promising youngsters within their grasp are not tempted away.

Given that Wales are working with limited resources, the loss of any player - particularly one who has been nurtured in their system - is something the FAW is desperate to avoid.

"Our hope is that young female players who were born in Wales feel a sense of belonging to represent Cymru," Adams said.

articles.title: Jess Fishlock: Welsh legend aiming to keep career alive in NWSL play-offs
articles.summary: On Sunday, 1 November, Jess Fishlock takes to the pitch for Seattle Reign against Orlando Pride, not knowing if it will be her final match.
articles.body:
On Sunday, 1 November, Wales legend Jess Fishlock will take to the pitch for Seattle Reign against Orlando Pride, not knowing whether it will be her final match.

The Reign, the club Fishlock has called home since 2013, are competing with NC Courage and Denver Summit for the final National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) play-off spot.

Beat Orlando, and Seattle - with whom the 39-year-old has won three NWSL Shields - guarantee an eighth play-off berth in Fishlock's 14-season stint in Washington state.

NC Courage and Denver Summit boast a higher goal difference than Reign and sit two and three points behind them respectively, but face each other on the final day.

"I've been in this league long enough to understand how this works. I think we've had a couple of situations like this before," said Fishlock.

"The beauty of it is you just get to focus on football, which is ultimately all we want to do as players.

"All I want to do is get this group into another round of play-offs and see what happens after that. There's a lot going on, which is so fun and so exciting."

Wales in fight to retain rising female stars

Fishlock called an end to her international career in October 2025, having represented Wales 166 times - a record for men and women.

She signed a new contract in Seattle a month later, before confirming in April that she would retire at the conclusion of the 2026 NWSL campaign.

Fishlock has never won the NWSL play-offs, finishing as runner-up on three separate occasions in 2014, 2015 and, most recently, in 2023.

Progression to the eight-team knockout stage would extend her glittering club career, which includes two Champions League titles, and offer the chance to bow out in style.

Reign will honour the veteran midfielder, with several activities planned around the stadium, including a commemorative photo booth and dedicated merchandise.

Several members of Fishlock's family have flown out to the Pacific Northwest so they can be among the expected 16,000-strong crowd at Lumen Field.

"I don't think I've had this many family out, ever. It's been a little crazy," Fishlock added.

"I'm not used to having little Rugrats running around everywhere, taking all of my spare energy that I need. But it's been great.

"I will really be able to enjoy it post-game. I'm focusing on the match itself and [reaching the] playoffs to keep the season going a little bit longer, which would be nice.

"I'm extremely grateful and so appreciative of everybody showing out for me. Everything that the Reign has done has been undeniably incredible and beautiful.

"But without sounding ungrateful, I am still very much focused on the game itself. I'm sure post everything, it will hit me far harder than I'm allowing it to hit me right now."

Fishlock's retirement will close a chapter in Reign's history, as she is the last of the club's original three stars to step away, following Megan Rapinoe and Lauren Barnes.

It will also mark the end of an era for the league. She is one of the division's most recognisable figures, and bounced back from a serious-looking injury to go out on her own terms.

Hanging up her boots will afford Fishlock, who is always vocal about her Welsh pride, the chance to return home much more often.

The next visit to Wales is in the diary, as she will return to the national team as part of Rhian Wilkinson's coaching staff for their World Cup play-off final against Norway.

Before Wales' semi-final triumph over Albania, Wilkinson revealed a message sent to her by Fishlock urging the boss to "call her up".

Fishlock noted that her message was tongue-in-cheek, and knows that Wilkinson would not call upon her for another Wales bow, despite injury concerns.

"I know that Rhian would not do that to me, bless her. She is too understanding as a coach. That message was in jest, and she understood that," Fishlock added.

"I'm excited for Wales and their game against Norway. I believe they can do it, and I hope that they believe they can do it."

articles.title: Lincoln Riley claps back at critics with fiery postgame written statement
articles.summary: After USC beat Ohio State, Lincoln Riley pulled out a written statement that was a clear dig at all the noise surrounding the Trojans.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES — If you didn't think Lincoln Riley paid a single second to all of the critics calling for his demise , wait until you see how he ended his victory news conference.

For the nine minutes he sat inside the interview room inside the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum, the Southern California coach was poised and timid when talking about the statement win over No. 2 Ohio State , seemingly downplaying the significance of his first top five victory with the Trojans .

But before he walked away from the podium, he took out a piece of paper − which he seemingly wrote something on − and read it out and a clear dig at everyone who doubted if he was the right man for USC.

"I wanted to make sure to articulate my thoughts," he said. "This program is built on internal joy, not external applause. This wins for all the staff members, the players, the leaders, admin, all the people within the walls.

"I said before this game that I'm the right person for this job, and as long as all those people know that, that's all I care about. I appreciate being a part of this university and all it does. I appreciate our kids and our staff, and I'm going to continue to fight on because that's what being a Trojan is all about."

He then said "adios" and got up − making sure he got one last word in after the time for reporters to ask questions ended.

After the questionable loss to Wisconsin in Week 8, media and fans across the country pondered if this was the last stand of Riley as it seemed USC was about to fall short of its lofty College Football Playoff expectations. USA TODAY Sports reported on Tuesday, Oct. 27 Riley and USC are in an "unhappy marriage," as "both sides know" it's not a good fit, according to people with direct insight into the Trojans.

He faced plenty of questions throughout the week leading up to Week 9, defending that he wants to be at USC and believes he is the right guy to be in charge while focusing on the Buckeyes. In a must-win game, his team came out and took down Ohio State in impressive fashion, taking the lead on the second play of the game and never looking back in a 30-18 victory that keeps the Trojans alive in the playoff hunt.

Riley's players also backed up their coach's sentiment after learning what he said.

"The outside noise it don't affect us," said defensive end Braylan Shelby. "Everybody can say what they want to say about us. They can say this and that, but internally, it's all about us. It's always been about us, so we keep striving. Like I said, each and every day, we're gonna get greatness in production on the field. We don't listen to outside noise, but we listen to internal noise, and that's what feeds us and drives us."

As he fielded question after question, Riley seemed humble and out to be the better person.

But he just couldn't resist clapping back at the haters.

articles.title: 2 Up, 2 Down: Sunderland’s Woes Deepen As Coventry Emerge Victorious
articles.summary: From bad, to worse, to…terminal? Our writers react to a Halloween horror at the CBS Arena.
articles.body:
I'm not saying we were unlucky at all but they did score three times from four shots on target — two of which took deflections — and they had an xG of 0.67, so if we're looking for any positives, maybe it wasn't as bad as it felt.

There were also twenty minutes in the second half when we looked OK. Far too late, but at least we didn't throw the towel in.

Enzo scored his penalty — it would've capped off the day if he'd missed.

We seem to be finding the self-destruct button far too easily and too often this season.

Gifting Coventry the first goal was the last thing we needed in the circumstances. We then did the same thing for the second, gifting them the ball to make it pretty much "game over" before half time. I wouldn't have minded so much if we were played off the park, but that wasn't the case and Coventry benefitted from so pretty woeful defending.

We weren't any better going forward either, with Brian Brobbey missing the only decent chance created in the first half. He should've scored as well.

The lack of urgency and fight from the start was really worrying — as if the players, or the head coach, don't realise how serious this is now looking.

Brighton and Bournemouth had all the hallmarks of a team in a relegation battle. If Régis Le Bris doesn't realise, he needs to go. If he can't get that over to the players and get a response from them, he needs to go.

It would be incredibly sad and tough on him if they do sack him.

I think he might get the Chelsea game to save his skin, but what do I know?

I didn't think we were that bad in the first half.

Now, I'm very much an optimist when it comes to Sunderland and I had high hopes of a comfortable victory. Maybe it's my fault we lost as I had a bet on Sunderland to win and Brian Brobbey to score. I do think we at least matched them first half and we weren't deserving of a two goal deficit at half time.

Yes, I'm afraid not being quite as shite as it sounds is one of my positives.

The subs were a positive but we should've been changing things at half time for me.

I'm baffled by swapping a right back for a right back at 3-1 down regardless of whether Thomas Meunier played as a right back. For me, Jocelin Ta Bi had to come on at half time and even with the more attacking setup, we didn't look like getting back into that at any point.

Has Régis Le Bris run out of ideas or is he being stubborn about not playing on the front foot?

Either way, he's on borrowed time and I never thought I'd have one foot in that camp. If he survives the weekend, I imagine he has to go balls out for the next couple of games, or he's toast.

It might be my positive attitude again, but why, whenever we make a mistake, does it always fall straight to the opposition and then cost us dearly?

If that happens while we're attacking, somehow the ball gets smuggled away and we don't get a shot off. It didn't seem to be like that last season…what's changed?

Whatever it is, I'm £30 down and as disillusioned as I've been in a long time.

I'm sure that Régis Le Bris would've sent his side out with instructions to avoid defensive errors and not to concede the first goal.

These mistakes at the back have been haunting us and is why we're struggling in the Premier League. Omar Alderete looked frustrated throughout and has left us with more problems at the back with his late dismissal.

Dan Ballard's influence is being missed.

The second goal for Coventry was down to weak tackling in the centre of defence, with Luke O'Nien being robbed too easily.

Robin Roefs was often making his feelings known to the players in front of him, and deflections didn't help him for two of the goals. But overall, just not good enough.

The impact of the substitutions was remarkable — Chemsdine Talbi had a shot just wide ahead of the penalty decision.

The third Coventry goal made life very difficult, as psychologically it would've been much easier to come back from 2-1 behind, but at least Sunderland put in a decent shift in the second half and had a number of good chances.

Coventry bring more motivation to their game

When a team is at the bottom of the league, the minimum the fans expect is a battling performance, and we did see some of that after the substitutes came on.

But it seemed that Coventry were often more switched on than we were, especially in the first half. The home team were clinical in front of goal.

Just as winning becomes a habit, so does losing.

The general hesitancy which was completely absent in the winning team display versus Brentford in midweek was back again, on a day when we needed points.

To be fair, Coventry did play well, but with each loss, tensions rise, and we need a win very soon.

When Trai Hume got behind the ball, with the goal gaping and Carl Rushworth stranded on the floor, it felt like a golden chance that we needed to take.

Sadly, in the Premier League, it's been the first half of the story of our season and the second half of our story followed soon after with some absolutely criminal defending.

Last season, when we went behind, there was a genuine feeling of resilience and that we simply wouldn't roll over and accept the result. This season couldn't be more of the opposite — we looked crestfallen and then proceeded to accept an absolute battering.

Any human being with basic function could've seen at half time that our plan wasn't working and that changes needed to be made. Why, then, did the same team come out for the second half?

As much as it's a cliché, had we started the second half with more attacking impetus at 2-0 down, we could have recovered.

Allowing Coventry to score a third goal is just unacceptable. The players have let down Régis le Bris and themselves in a disappointingly familiar tale.

I can't believe I'm saying this given the highs we've experienced with Le Bris, but it's so vital that we retain our status in the Premier League.

Persisting with poor selections such as Chris Rigg and Trai Hume on our right side, along with not acknowledging the horrendous form of our midfield, is making me question if a change is needed.

Honestly, I'd be devastated if Le Bris was to leave, but these players are simply not performing to the standards needed. They're putting his job at risk, but his tactical selections aren't helping proceedings, either.

A good penalty from Enzo Le Fée and scoreline comforts

Nerves of steel on a shit day. We also lost by one less than the pricks up the road so I'll take that.

Not good enough, and too many errors for about the fifth game or more this season.

Shocking performances and major step ups needed, and as if the defensive errors weren't enough, Omar Alderete getting sent off as he did late on is absolutely stupid.

The problems at the back are now amplified and we have a hell of a lot of games coming up. Drop him and promote someone who has a brain.

With the names we have in the middle, we should be embarrassed at that showing.

We didn't win anywhere near enough first or second balls; we were out-fought and they simply wanted it more.

The lads knocking on the door from midweek including in the middle and out wide were given no chance to help either.

I'll be eternally grateful for what Régis Le Bris has done and he'll always be a special part of our history, but that wasn't good enough — 2-0 down at half time with a raft of talent on the bench, he changed zero at half time, and we were 3-0 down by the time he made any changes.

If he can't adjust quickly enough and can't give the multi-millions worth of talent we have a go or can't get the best out if them, maybe now's the time to move on.

He's the best manager we have had in decades but he has fallen into the same trap as Peter Reid, being unable to kick on after laying a great platform

Time to move on, as much as it pains me.

Sunderland occasionally threaten in attack

On the rare occasions they had opportunities, I thought Nilson Angulo and Brian Brobbey were fairly bright.

Enzo Le Fee's penalty kick was a good one.

I haven't been particularly on board with the "his legs are gone" discourse, but yeah…his legs are gone and it was so, so obvious.

If the ball is two steps away, he's going to get beaten to it, and it's going to lead to a break. The back four is a disaster for a plethora of reasons, but Xhaka isn't doing them any favors.

Le Fee wasn't much better in the first half.

It's unfortunately time to say goodbye to Le Bris.

What he accomplished in his first two seasons was incredible, but right now he's trying the same thing over and over again and hasn't accepted it's not going to work.

Yes, the centre backs are a disaster, but he's not doing anything to hide the deficiency. Yes, Nordi Mukiele isn't available to spring the attack from right back, so play an actual attacking winger there.

That first half was crying out for changes at half time, but there were none until the third goal. He's stubbornly refusing to try something else and the club can't continue stubbornly refusing to make changes that need to be made.

Sunderland's players let themselves down

An absolutely disgraceful performance that should see every single one of them look into the mirror and ask themselves if they really want to play for this club and if they really have the backbone to get us out of this mess.

For almost the entire season, these players have played with an arrogance and an attitude that is not befitting of the club. To have sat on Wednesday and watched their team mates put in a performance full of vigour and bravery, and to then turn up to a game of this magnitude and play as they did is nothing short of abhorrent.

Every single player is culpable and every single player should hang their heads in shame. Disgraceful.

He's completely out of ideas and the uncomfortable truth is that he has been for weeks.

Since the first game of the season, we've played a style that hasn't suited a single individual player.

Wednesday night was welcomed by fans and rightly so, a return to the swashbuckling style that endeared this side to the fans, the high press, high energy and dynamic football brought out the very best in what was Sunderlands second string — why this was abandoned for this tepid, slow and pathetically weak style is anyone's guess.

Every game this season, we've set up to allow the opposition to settle, to let them get comfortable and ultimately punish us for our tepidness, and for what? Players out of position, others shown more loyalty than they're worthy of, and ultimately too many players being fed to the wolves.

Le Bris has given us some wonderful times but as he stood without reaction on the touchline, I was overcome by the feeling this was a manager who was fully out of ideas and for that reason, it's time for both parties to move on.

It's all wrong and it's been all wrong almost all season.

It's widely accepted that the best version of Sunderland is aggressive, front-foot, and full of energy. On Wednesday, we saw that return, but it's evident that was only a brief blip.

Questions should rightly be asked as to why we've chosen to chase a style that negates our strengths. It's slow, ponderous, without direction and allows teams to get a head start against us almost every game.

I'm also of the belief that this feeds into why we are making so many mistakes defensively; the passive, low-intensity play is making it too difficult for defenders to get into the pace of the game and so are continuously caught out by the opposition.

So far, this passive, boring and predominantly sideways football has yielded no gain to a squad of players that can't possibly enjoy playing like this.

Kyril Louis-Dreyfus now faces his toughest call as an owner. This football can't continue and its' becoming increasingly clear many fans are feeling the manager is now in above his head.

There are little signs of improvement forthcoming and this result confirmed beyond all doubt that not only are we in a relegation battle but that battle is an uphill one as we remain rooted to bottom of the table. The real risk for Dreyfus comes from the fact that if he doesn't pull the trigger soon and our fortunes don't change, when he does feel Le Bris is in an untenable position, it may well already be too late.

Questions also need asked about the large turnover of staff that has been a fixture of Le Bris' time at Sunderland and what impact that's had on a side that\s suffering from a real identity crisis, as well as the underwhelming summer in which Florent Ghisolfi was — on this evidence — incapable of providing any improvements to the squad.

Another weekend of more questions than answers and perhaps the fact we still haven't got answers to questions we've been asking for over a month tells its own story.
