articles.title: Régis Le Bris’ Red And White Empire Is In Danger Of Collapse
articles.summary: The under-pressure Lads’ boss saw his charges fail again on Saturday. Can he weather this storm and turn things around?
articles.body:
It wasn't inevitable. It wasn't written in the stars that following a season of timeless memories, iconic results and European football in the final reckoning, Sunderland would find themselves rock bottom of the Premier League after nine games of the 2026/2027 season, seemingly drifting aimlessly and struggling to generate any momentum.

To say the least, it's been a turnaround so stark, so painful and so mind-boggling that few of us may fully comprehend how quickly things have turned sour and may also not be geared up for what feels like a season of struggle — but it's the current reality at Sunderland and there can be no hiding place.

Cite statistical quirks and mitigating factors as much as you like, but the league table doesn't lie and we're currently in a real hole. Optimism is always a virtue but "Keep the faith" rings extremely hollowly when you're in this position, and we should know that as well as any fanbase you could name.

The habit is one of losing, goals are almost non-existent, and player morale appears to be dipping as well. To this writer's wizened eye, it feels all too familiar; the kind of struggle we endured on an almost seasonal basis between 2007 and 2017…and we know how that ended.

Saturday's loss to Coventry — the latest half-arsed, disjointed stumble to defeat amid a run of throughly underwhelming league results for the Lads this season — was perhaps the most painful reverse yet.

With absolutely no disrespect to Frank Lampard and his players, there's a creeping realisation that we aren't the team we were but that at present, we're a rabble; a group of out-of-form players being led by a head coach that seems lost and short of ideas. It's embarrassing and it's an indictment of how badly things have gone wrong since that iconic victory over Chelsea, but this league is merciless and we're not the first club to get it wrong on such a scale.

Was it expecting too much for Sunderland to at least try and build on last season's seventh-place finish?

I really don't think it was, and if we can't crack the top flight with this setup and structure, I'd be doubtful as to whether we ever will. Maybe a three or four-place drop, given the added demands of this season, would've been tolerable, but to slide from seventh to twentieth? Absolutely not.

It may be tough to accept, but this is real.

This is what and who we are right now: a painfully average, blunt, listless group of players marshalled by a captain whose legs appear unresponsive and whose teammates don't seem capable of finding the solutions to the problems.

We hyped these lads to the moon last season and rightly so, but they're finding out the hard way that the red and white stripes can weigh heavily on even the most powerful shoulders when things start to slide. Can they somehow find the minerals and the fighting spirit to respond, to overturn this wretched run of form and begin to haul Sunderland out of the mire? It feels unlikely at this stage, you'd have to say.

On Le Bris, the paradox is most interesting.

He doesn't deserve the flak he's currently taking and it goes without saying that this classy, charismatic and composed figure will always be revered in Sunderland for the heights to which he's taken us, but at the moment, he's a man under immense pressure and for whom the solutions don't seem to be presenting themselves.

He's most certainly being let down by his players (the standards he implemented upon his arrival in 2024 have dropped alarmingly and the players' attitudes haven't seemed right all season, of that there's no doubt), but he's not totally without fault, either.

If Leeds and Brentford were deemed steps forward, with Sunderland showing flashes of their potential and Jocelin Ta Bi and Jules Ahoka standing out, Saturday's collapse at the CBS was a massive step backwards as the formation became confused, belief was almost non-existent and the red and white defence crumbled alarmingly under pressure.

Simply put, nothing he's trying in the league is working and although Europa League football seems to be to our liking, the story is altogether more gruesome closer to home and with every league game that goes by, nerves and tension are starting to permeate every aspect of the matchday experience.

Can he survive? Will he be given time? I don't want to see such a transformative figure lose his job and leave Sunderland on the flattest of notes, but this feels like an all-too-familiar scenario, like a movie you've watched countless times and still find yourself hoping that this time, the ending will be different and your favourite hero will survive against the odds.

In the span of two years, Le Bris has built something special at Sunderland. At this moment, it feels like it's on the brink of collapse — and what a sad ending that could ultimately prove to be.

Notre Dame Fighting Irish vs. Navy Midshipmen: Head-To-Head Record

Despite being one of the most talked-about fixtures of the independents, the head-to-head record has been lopsided, with the Fighting Irish cruising ahead in wins.

Despite Notre Dame's overwhelming historical success, today's first half shows the Navy Midshipmen can still challenge the Fighting Irish.

articles.title: Centre Hawkins determined to make World Cup
articles.summary: Wales centre Joe Hawkins says missing the previous World Cup has made him more determined to make the next global tournament in Australia in 12 months.
articles.body:
Wales centre Joe Hawkins says missing the previous World Cup has made him more determined to make the next global tournament in Australia in 12 months.

Following his move from Ospreys to Exeter in 2023, Hawkins was deemed ineligible to play for Wales by Welsh rugby's Professional Rugby Board (PRB) because of the 25-cap rule.

The rule says players who have fewer than 25 caps are unavailable to play for Wales if they are not involved with a Welsh club.

This ruled him out of the 2023 World Cup in France but Hawkins has since returned to the national side after signing for Scarlets.

"I have no regrets," said 24-year-old Hawkins.

"It would have been nice to have a World Cup under my belt already, but that just makes me even more excited for potentially what's ahead over the next year.

"I loved my couple of years in Exeter with the life experience and playing in the Prem, where you can see a lot of the boys are thriving in now."

Wales have a minimum of 12 matches before the World Cup, starting with the Nations Championship opener against Japan in Cardiff next Saturday.

"It's always in the back of your mind, knowing you're going into a World Cup year," said Hawkins.

"You can probably see from performances from other boys in all positions in the squads that in a World Cup year, the intensity probably rises at the clubs.

"Boys are playing for positions and knowing that's the carrot at the end of the year.

"But if you're not taking care of the here and now you're not going to get that far."

Hawkins, 24, and Scarlets partner Eddie James have developed as Wales' first-choice centre pairing during the past 12 months.

Wales head coach Steve Tandy has selected five different starting midfield partnerships in 13 games since taking charge in September 2025.

Hawkins and James are the most prolific pair, having been together for seven games which include victory in an uncapped match against Barbarians.

Tandy did go back to Ben Thomas and Max Llewellyn for the 43-0 defeat by South Africa in July, but the Scarlets pair have been the preferred option.

"Eddie and I have a good relationship on and off the field," said Hawkins.

"That is starting to grow on the pitch with the more opportunities we get together."

The make-up of the Wales midfield has caused debate with Tandy and attack coach Matt Sherratt wanting a creative ball-playing inside centre like Hawkins or Thomas.

This leaves James as the physical presence at outside centre with Tandy stating he sees the Carmarthen-born 24-year-old's long-term future as a Test 13.

Many observers believe James should be considered as a 12 but Wales are determined to keep their creative options open.

With Thomas missing because of a calf injury, Hawkins appears to be competing for the Wales' 12 jersey with uncapped Dragons centre Aneurin Owen, although Llewellyn has also featured at inside centre for Gloucester this season.

"The ball-playing stuff is stuff I enjoy doing but you still need to go forward as well and I feel like I can also produce that side of it," said Hawkins.

"Matt [Sherratt] likes you always in and around that first receiver position so you are always in those decision-making roles.

"You've got to be comfortable on the ball and making decisions at high speed.

"But there's not always going to be opportunities to ball play, so you've got to try and have a bit of a rounded game."

Hawkins has also been employed as an outside-half by Scarlets but he sees his future at 12.

"It gives me a lot more respect for the 10s, having been in there, with all the work they do," he added.

"It probably helps me when I play centre from being a 10, I know what they need from me a little bit more, so the information and communication I'm feeding helps the whole team."

articles.title: Hansi Flick reveals 'easy' secret to Lamine Yamal substitution as Barcelona crush Alaves
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal scored twice as Barcelona bounced back from consecutive defeats with a dominant 6-1 victory over Alaves in Liga. Manager Hansi Flick praised his...
articles.body:
Lamine Yamal scored twice as Barcelona bounced back from consecutive defeats with a dominant 6-1 victory over Alaves in Liga. Manager Hansi Flick praised his attacking stars after the emphatic response, while also explaining the decision to substitute his teenage sensation late in the game.

Yamal and Raphinha both scored twice as Barcelona secured an emphatic 6-1 Liga victory over Alaves on Saturday. Fermin Lopez and Anthony Gordon were also on the scoresheet during a dominant performance at Camp Nou.

The comprehensive win provided the perfect response for Hansi Flick's side. It came immediately after their impressive 11-game winning streak was halted by back-to-back defeats against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid . Mariano Diaz managed a late consolation for the visitors, but Barca were already out of sight following a ruthless attacking display.

Flick explains Yamal substitution decision

Yamal has enjoyed a remarkable workload this season, starting all 18 matches for Barcelona and Spain. However, Flick was finally able to offer the teenager a brief rest, substituting him for the final 20 minutes against Alaves with the game already won. The Barcelona boss explained that the winger's decisive impact made the substitution much smoother.

"When you score two goals, it's easier to go out," Flick admitted after taking the forward off for only the fourth time this season. "I spoke with him at half time. For us, that he has the confidence back with the one vs. one situations, more time and minutes in the second half is good, but it also important he has less minutes."

Attacking stars deliver perfect response

The hosts wasted no time establishing their dominance, with Raphinha opening the scoring early on. Lopez quickly doubled the advantage before Raphinha netted his 17th goal of the campaign to make it 3-0.

Yamal then added the fourth before half-time, capping off a superb team move from the edge of the penalty area. He grabbed his second of the game after the interval with a delicate dinked finish that was initially ruled out for offside.

Flick was thrilled with the collective effort from his forward line, saying: "For Lamine it was a great game, but it was good to see the level of the attack: Fermin, Rapha. This is what I want to see after these two defeats. How we react, it was good and in the right way."

Following their emphatic return to form in Liga, Barc must now shift their focus back to European competition. Aston Villa are set to visit Camp Nou for a crucial Champions League clash on Tuesday.

The demanding schedule will then continue with a massive top-of-the-table fixture next weekend. Flick's squad will travel to face Atletico Madrid in a highly anticipated league showdown. These two significant fixtures will define the club's momentum heading into the upcoming international break.

articles.title: Williams heart warning after career ended at 22
articles.summary: At just 22, Keelan Williams faced the hardest decision of his life as stage one heart failure made him call an end to his football career.
articles.body:
At just 22 years old, Keelan Williams faced the hardest decision of his life. Stage one heart failure caused him to call an end to his football career.

After two open-heart surgeries and two pacemaker implants, the former Liverpool and Burnley academy prospect had exhausted his medical options.

Williams was diagnosed with a bicuspid aortic valve - a congenital condition in which the valve has two flaps instead of three - at the age of 15.

But seven years later, further complications forced him to quit the sport both he and his older brother, Wales international Neco Williams, had dreamed of playing professionally since childhood.

"It's sad and disappointing that I've had to make the decision to retire and step away from playing because of a cardiac condition," Williams told BBC Sport.

Williams' football journey started at local side Cefn United, before he joined a Liverpool satellite academy at six and signed terms with the Reds at eight.

He remained in Liverpool's academy until 16, when he joined Burnley, all while representing Welsh youth teams up to under-19s level.

Spells at then Cymru Premier side Bala Town and Cymru North club Denbigh Town followed before medical advice prompted an early retirement.

Although stepping away has left Williams wondering what might have been, the support he has received and his brother's continued success have helped him adjust to life away from football.

"It's always a privilege to chase something you've always dreamed of alongside your brother, who has made it now," Williams added.

"Neco is doing so well. I think he is the best full-back in the Premier League. That's what keeps me going, really."

Williams also highlights the "crazy" love and backing he has received from family and friends, along with the level of support he has had through social media.

"It's something that I don't take for granted. I really treasure the support. It would be much more difficult if I didn't have that.

"Football is all about setbacks and how you respond. I've had to stop playing completely, which is more extreme, but you have to look at the positives."

It was during a Wales Under-16s camp that his heart condition was first discovered. Before a trip abroad, every squad member had to undergo a routine check-up.

"Wales thought that they had found a murmur in my heart, so they stopped me from travelling until further check-ups were made," Williams recalled.

"They referred me to Broadgreen Hospital [in Liverpool], where they found that I had an aortic bicuspid valve and I had a slight leak in the valve.

"They noticed this without me getting any symptoms. I had no symptoms whatsoever.

"I was lucky in many senses that I played for Liverpool and Wales because if I didn't, I may have never known that I had a leak in my valve."

Initially, the discovery did not impact Williams' burgeoning career. As long as he did not experience symptoms, he could continue to play as normal.

After departing Burnley's academy, the then 20-year-old joined Bala in January 2024 as he sought to continue his career closer to home.

By the end of the year, his life had changed.

Following a routine check-up, Williams was told the leak in his heart valve had worsened, and that surgery was now required.

In January 2025, Williams underwent valve-sparing aortic root replacement surgery, followed by a dual-chamber pacemaker implantation.

But complications meant he was admitted to an intensive care unit (ICU) and treated for sepsis, a collapsed lung and respiratory failure.

After 11 days in ICU, Williams recovered and underwent a second, successful operation in September 2025, which he hoped would allow him to continue playing.

"When I got back, I couldn't perform at 100%. I would sprint up the pitch, and I'd feel gassed, out of breath, and my legs were heavy," he said.

"Initially, I thought it was my fitness after returning from a second heart surgery.

"But I had heart failure. My ejection fracture percentage was only 37%, meaning my heart was not pumping as well as it should be."

Most fit and healthy adults will have a left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) that ranges between 50% and 70%.

Williams was given medication to combat his LVEF - he now takes five tablets every day - and was fitted with an upgraded pacemaker.

"I still didn't feel 100%. Again, I thought it was my fitness, but I was still feeling the same two months later when I should have been back to normal."

A recent echocardiogram showed practically no sign of improvement. Williams' LVEF had only increased to 38%.

"That's when I decided that I will have to stop playing because I couldn't carry on physically with how I felt," he said.

Williams is living with many of the complications linked to stage-one heart failure and regularly attends heart failure, cardiology and pacemaker clinics.

The entire family has been tested for the same condition, with no signs of a heart condition found in any other member.

And the Williams family sleep a little easier knowing that Keelan's condition was spotted at the earliest stage.

Now he would like to see footballers across all levels of the pyramid seeking out their own check-ups, even if their clubs do not currently offer them.

"Football clubs at the highest level will, these days, offer everyone routine heart checks, but those with fewer resources might not," he said.

"To anyone out there, I would 100% get your heart checked to be on the safe side. You want to find it as soon as possible, as I did."

articles.title: Wales in fight to retain rising female stars
articles.summary: Wales face an "increasingly aggressive" battle to secure the international futures of talented youngsters tempted to switch to England.
articles.body:
Wales are facing a fight to hold on to some of their most promising female footballers amid an "increasingly aggressive" battle to secure the international futures of talented youngsters.

Wales have already lost rising Manchester United star Layla Drury, the Wrexham-born forward who became the Red Devils' youngest ever female goalscorer in January.

Drury, 17, switched allegiances to England earlier this year having previously represented Wales at under-17 level.

The loss of Drury, who has already played eight times for United's first team, was a heavy blow for Wales given her potential and the fact that she was part of the Football Association of Wales' (FAW) development system.

The concern for the FAW is that further young Welsh talents could be tempted to switch allegiances, with the pull of a potential Lionesses career regarded as significant.

"The market for capturing and retaining talent has become increasingly aggressive," FAW chief football officer David Adams told BBC Sport Wales.

"We must make every effort to protect our assets and retain our top talent to protect the future success of the women's national teams."

Since 2020, the FAW has focused attempts to develop young female players - aged between 11 and 16 - on programmes in north and south Wales.

As part of the system, a group of 31 players are involved in three training sessions a week and play games in the FAW's National Academi boys' set-up in order to aid their development.

There is a further pool of 50 players who compete in Adran Premier academies and train with the FAW's girls' development set-up twice a week, while Wales-qualified girls at English academies are invited to a school holiday regional programme.

The FAW's development programme, which has been awarded Fifa academy status, also focuses on analysis work and strength and conditioning in an attempt to produce future Wales internationals.

A high proportion of players involved are either dual-qualified or have multi-national heritage.

The fact that many of those players are likely to sign for clubs in England when aged 15 to 16 – with no top-class women's clubs to join in Wales – can be problematic for the FAW.

If players are representing English clubs, they are more likely to come to the attention of those working in England's international pathway.

The opportunity to play for England is viewed as appealing for some players because they are one of the women's game's heavyweight sides, having won the Women's Euros twice in a row and reached the Women's World Cup final in 2023.

As well as the increased chance of success on the pitch, playing for the Lionesses can bring significant commercial opportunities for individual players.

Unlike the men's game, where the biggest financial rewards are on offer at club level, the commercial side of playing international football can be a significant pull for some female players because of the far lower salaries paid at women's clubs.

Former captain Kath Morgan won 51 caps during a 14-year Wales career and has also coached the national side.

She currently coaches Welsh youngsters at Coleg y Cymoedd's full-time female academy and also works as an agent for some players, including new Wales cap Casi Gregson.

Morgan believes young players are driven primarily by a desire to become professionals – and will go wherever it takes to make that happen.

"I don't think it's a decision based on finances - I think it's more based on the chance to have success in their careers," Morgan said.

While there is an acceptance that competing with England's resources is not possible, Morgan argues there is a need for further investment in girls' football in Wales.

"There has to be consistency in creating the pathway," she added.

"The crux of it is that if there's a lack of infrastructure and investment, players will inevitably go to where that is offered."

A hope that players feel 'sense of belonging'

Manchester City centre-back Mayzee Davies, 20, 19-year-old Manchester United full-back Scarlett Hill and United attacking midfielder Mared Griffiths, also 19, have all broken into Rhian Wilkinson's Wales side having been part of the FAW's development system.

Had Drury opted for Wales, the likelihood is that she would also have at least one senior Welsh cap to her name by now, particularly after injuries forced Wilkinson to turn to a number of youngsters for last month's Women's World Cup semi-final games against Albania.

In truth, Drury – like club colleague Griffiths - might already be an international regular had she stuck with Wales.

Instead, she will hope an England senior chance comes at some point in the future having been a late addition to their U20 Women's World Cup squad in September.

Unless there is a change in Fifa regulations, there is no chance of Drury playing for Wales further down the line even if she does not become a Lioness.

The rules state that if a player features in a competitive game for one country – as Drury did for Wales Under-17s – they are allowed only one switch of nationality.

Vera Jones is another highly regarded Welsh-born teenager who is playing for England, though her situation is different.

The attacking midfielder, 18, spent five years in Barry Town's academy before joining Chelsea in 2024.

Currently on loan at Watford, Jones made her England Under-17 debut in 2023 and has remained part of the English set-up, featuring alongside Drury in the U20 Women's World Cup squad.

The difference in Jones' case is that she did not play for Wales before committing to England.

As a result she would – potentially - be eligible to switch to the land of her birth if she does not go on to play senior football for the Lionesses.

Whether that ever becomes a conversation depends on Jones' progress in the English system – as well as her wishes, of course - but Wales are sure to monitor the situation knowing she could one day follow the likes of Hannah Cain and Lois Joel by playing senior football for them having represented England at youth level.

In the meantime, Welsh football's bosses must do all they can to try to ensure the various promising youngsters within their grasp are not tempted away.

Given that Wales are working with limited resources, the loss of any player - particularly one who has been nurtured in their system - is something the FAW is desperate to avoid.

"Our hope is that young female players who were born in Wales feel a sense of belonging to represent Cymru," Adams said.

articles.title: Fishlock out to keep career alive in NWSL play-offs
articles.summary: On Sunday, 1 November, Jess Fishlock takes to the pitch for Seattle Reign against Orlando Pride, not knowing if it will be her final match.
articles.body:
On Sunday, 1 November, Wales legend Jess Fishlock will take to the pitch for Seattle Reign against Orlando Pride, not knowing whether it will be her final match.

Reign, the club Fishlock has called home since 2013, are competing with NC Courage and Denver Summit for the final National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) play-off spot.

Beat Orlando, and Seattle - with whom the 39-year-old has won three NWSL Shields - guarantee an eighth play-off berth in Fishlock's 14-season stint in Washington state.

NC Courage and Denver Summit boast a higher goal difference than Reign and sit two and three points behind them respectively, but face each other on the final day.

"I've been in this league long enough to understand how this works. I think we've had a couple of situations like this before," said Fishlock.

"The beauty of it is you just get to focus on football, which is ultimately all we want to do as players.

"All I want to do is get this group into another round of play-offs and see what happens after that. There's a lot going on, which is so fun and so exciting."

Fishlock called an end to her international career in October 2025, having represented Wales 166 times - a record for men and women.

She signed a new contract in Seattle a month later, before confirming in April that she would retire at the conclusion of the 2026 NWSL campaign.

Fishlock has never won the NWSL play-offs, finishing as runner-up on three separate occasions in 2014, 2015 and, most recently, in 2023.

Progression to the eight-team knockout stage would extend her glittering club career, which includes two Champions League titles, and offer the chance to bow out in style.

Reign will honour the veteran midfielder, with several activities planned around the stadium, including a commemorative photo booth and dedicated merchandise.

Several members of Fishlock's family have flown out to the Pacific Northwest so they can be among the expected 16,000-strong crowd at Lumen Field.

"I don't think I've had this many family out, ever. It's been a little crazy," Fishlock added.

"I'm not used to having little Rugrats running around everywhere, taking all of my spare energy that I need. But it's been great.

"I will really be able to enjoy it post-game. I'm focusing on the match itself and [reaching the] playoffs to keep the season going a little bit longer, which would be nice.

"I'm extremely grateful and so appreciative of everybody showing out for me. Everything that the Reign has done has been undeniably incredible and beautiful.

"But without sounding ungrateful, I am still very much focused on the game itself. I'm sure post everything, it will hit me far harder than I'm allowing it to hit me right now."

Fishlock's retirement will close a chapter in Reign's history, as she is the last of the club's original three stars to step away, following Megan Rapinoe and Lauren Barnes.

It will also mark the end of an era for the league. She is one of the division's most recognisable figures, and bounced back from a serious-looking injury to go out on her own terms.

Hanging up her boots will afford Fishlock, who is always vocal about her Welsh pride, the chance to return home much more often.

The next visit to Wales is in the diary, as she will return to the national team as part of Rhian Wilkinson's coaching staff for their World Cup play-off final against Norway.

Before Wales' semi-final triumph over Albania, Wilkinson revealed a message sent to her by Fishlock urging the boss to "call her up".

Fishlock noted that her message was tongue-in-cheek, and knows that Wilkinson would not call upon her for another Wales bow, despite injury concerns.

"I know that Rhian would not do that to me, bless her. She is too understanding as a coach. That message was in jest, and she understood that," Fishlock added.

"I'm excited for Wales and their game against Norway. I believe they can do it, and I hope that they believe they can do it."

Andoni Iraola's side are on a five-game unbeaten run in all competitions after beating Chelsea on penalties in the Carabao Cup in midweek.

articles.title: Anfield, intensity and rotations - how Iraola is improving Liverpool
articles.summary: Liverpool fans are finding joy at Anfield again with a feel-good factor around the club before the visit of reigning champions Arsenal on Sunday.
articles.body:
You have go back to 2012 for the last time Arsenal won a game at Anfield.

In recent years - whenever this fixture comes around - it is well-documented that Mikel Arteta was playing for the Gunners that day.

Arteta is now a Premier League-winning manager and leading reigning champions who will arrive at Anfield on Sunday (16:30 GMT) hoping to end that streak.

But they will come up against a Liverpool side starting to find some rhythm under Andoni Iraola and with backing from a re-energised Anfield crowd.

Since tasting their only defeat of the season so far against Manchester City on 11 October, Liverpool have won their past five across all competitions.

Not since the start of last season under Arne Slot have they had such a run. Facing Arsenal at the end of a week in which the Gunners were knocked out of the Carabao Cup by League Two Fleetwood, they will sense an opportunity to deliver a statement to the rest of the Premier League.

Former Reds defender Jamie Carragher believes Liverpool are the biggest title challengers to Arsenal, , external though, speaking on Friday, Iraola insisted it was too early to look at the table.

Either way, the game will offer an early indication of Liverpool 's progress under the Basque boss.

Victory will mean them move just three points behind Arsenal , but defeat would mean the difference extends to nine points after nine games.

For vast parts of last season, Anfield lost its fear factor and watching Liverpool became a turgid experience. In the past fortnight, the connection between the fanbase and the side seems to have grown again.

Liverpool were flawed against Villarreal but the atmosphere was electric as they came from behind to win. The feel-good factor has only grown since, with an impressive win against high-flying Brighton in the Premier League and victory on penalties over Chelsea in the Carabao Cup.

"We have a big advantage over other teams because this atmosphere we can create is special," said Iraola.

Big-money signings like Alexander Isak, Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz are all heading in the right direction, while players like Cody Gakpo and Alexis Mac Allister have been much better this season than last.

At the back, Ronald Araujo is already a fan favourite and Jeremy Jacquet has seamlessly settled into the Premier League. Iraola's growing trust in using youngsters like Rio Ngumoha, Trey Nyoni, Lewis Koumas and James McConnell is certainly worth highlighting too.

Liverpool have made three or more starting XI changes in nine consecutive games and that rotation has been a key aspect of Iraola's own adaptation to coaching two games a week.

"It's true that [when I came], I didn't have a lot of experience [coaching two games a week], but I had a lot as a player of when you arrive back at 3am in the morning and so on," said Iraola.

"It's different to managing, but you do a lot of the job with the analysts, in the video room with the board and without spending the legs but I think our players are very used to it so a lot of the work is done.

"Now, it's more a matter of getting the decisions right, in terms of loading and freshening the legs. We are changing [the team] a lot from game to game and I think we will continue this approach."

Iraola is a believer that possession itself is not overly important but he wants his team to produce the better chances.

"Whoever controls the game is whoever controls the chances," he said, after Liverpool 's 2-0 win over Brighton , where the Reds only had the ball for 35.6% of the playing time.

Liverpool went more direct against a Brighton side that like to keep the ball and it worked. Liverpool are averaging 24.9 long balls per Premier League game this season, compared to 21 last term.

In terms of high pressures in the opposition half (165.9 per game, compared to 160.1) and sprints (128.3 per game, compared to 123.2), Iraola's side are doing more in comparison to last season but they are actually covering marginally less distance (111.1 km per game, compared to 111.7km)

Asked what has changed under Iraola, captain Virgil van Dijk offered an interesting response earlier this week.

"The 'intensity' word has been said so many times, sometimes a bit of chaos and there is this risk-reward that's going on now as well," he said.

"If we press high, I ended up at one point almost putting Cody [Gakpo] in one versus one on goal when I intercepted the ball on the right-hand side - when I'm a left centre-back. It's this sort of intensity that we try to get into our press.

"It's still a work in progress, but if you defend with a lot of intensity you have a big chance to win the ball high. Sometimes, that creates some risk and it could be vulnerable, but we're working on it a lot in order to be able to take that risk, but still not be as vulnerable as we have been sometimes."

There is more to come from the approach and Iraola insisted "there has to be another level" after arriving late to Friday's news conference because training overran.

If his side can find that, starting against Arsenal , then talk of a title challenge will only grow.

articles.title: Trent Alexander-Arnold: Real Madrid defender is struggling for minutes so where does his future lie?
articles.summary: Trent Alexander-Arnold is currently third-choice right-back at Real Madrid - where does his future lie?
articles.body:
It has not been an easy start to the season for Trent Alexander-Arnold.

The full-back joined Real Madrid in June 2025 with the ambition of establishing himself as the club's first-choice right-back, but the reality has been very different.

The arrival of Denzel Dumfries from Inter Milan this summer added more competition in the position, and now manager Jose Mourinho appears to be favouring Fede Valverde, normally a midfielder, as a starter at right-back.

It leaves Alexander-Arnold as third choice and leads to questions on where, and in what role, Mourinho sees the England international's future.

Alexander-Arnold has participated in seven of the 13 games Real have played this season, though he has only started four times and has made just one assist - in a 4-0 home win over Malaga.

And his involvement has notably declined over the past four games - he did not play against Roma, Sevilla or RB Leipzig and got just a couple of minutes in the Clasico, when he came on in stoppage time.

Alexander-Arnold has just turned 28 and Real showed how much they wanted him last summer by paying 10m euros (£8.33m) to secure his early release and make him available for the Club World Cup, rather than wait until he was available on a free transfer when his Liverpool contract expired.

But, despite having a contract until 2031, his future now hangs in the balance.

Alexander-Arnold made an excellent first impression at the club, winning over supporters during his first public appearance by delivering his arrival speech in Spanish and saying signing for Real was a "dream come true".

"I'm very happy and proud to be here. I'm eager to show the club and the fans what I can do," he added.

There was considerable optimism surrounding Alexander-Arnold's arrival, with his signing appearing to form part of the club's succession plan at right-back - he could provide cover for Dani Carvajal while positioning himself as a potential long-term successor to the veteran Spaniard.

His first season, however, fell short of expectations.

He made 21 La Liga appearances in 2025-26 out of a possible 38, with 14 starts, as injuries and a lack of continuity prevented Alexander-Arnold from establishing himself as a regular presence.

For a player arriving with his pedigree and reputation, it was a frustrating start to life in Madrid.

There have been several mitigating factors, and Alexander-Arnold is not the only player to have struggled to find his best form during a turbulent period for Real.

Firstly, injuries have played a significant role.

A hamstring problem in September and a thigh injury in December disrupted his first campaign and denied him the sustained run of games needed to build momentum and develop an understanding with his new team-mates, while a muscle issue during pre-season had already interrupted his preparations.

The turnover in management at the club hardly helped either. Xabi Alonso's departure and Alvaro Arbeloa's subsequent appointment meant Alexander-Arnold had to adapt to a change in leadership during his debut season.

Neither tenure brought the consistency Real had hoped for, while Mourinho now faces the task of finding the right balance within a squad packed with talent.

Mourinho has addressed speculation that Alexander-Arnold could leave Real Madrid in January, admitting that difficult selection decisions can be painful but insisting that the team's needs must come first.

"First of all, it hurts me. I don't like to make players feel bad. I want them to feel good," Mourinho said.

"Obviously, when you build a squad with two players per position as your foundation and then have a third player take the field, that's something I don't like.

"But there are things that are more important than these feelings. Things that are more important for the team at a given moment. And I decided that right now, the move was to change up the midfield and put Fede [Valverde] in there.

"But I was thinking about the team, not the players. Trent and Dumfries took it well when I explained that it was a decision for the team and not against the players."

Mourinho has previously highlighted Alexander-Arnold's versatility and tactical intelligence, insisting that squad rotation and positional flexibility will be crucial to Real's success.

Speaking at his first news conference in August, Mourinho stressed that competition for places would be important, naming Trent alongside Netherlands international Dumfries.

"It is not possible to think that one will play 60 games and the other none," he said, underlining the need to keep his squad involved and motivated.

That flexibility was evident against Inter Milan in September, when Mourinho deployed Alexander-Arnold in central midfield alongside Valverde because several midfield options were unavailable through suspension.

Mourinho was pleased with the defender's performance, saying he had "interpreted what he needed to really well, tactically" and that he and Valverde had "worked very well at this level".

Despite having to make difficult selection decisions, Mourinho has stressed the importance of keeping every member of his squad motivated and ready to contribute.

"Right now, we are working to make sure all the players are ready at all times, so everyone feels they could be playing and that they are important. That's very important for motivation."

Speaking on The Overlap, former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher said he would welcome Alexander-Arnold's return to the Merseyside club.

"I'd have him back," Carragher said. "He would get a lot of criticism, because I think he made a mistake. I think he made a big mistake going to Madrid.

"We've definitely missed his creativity."

Carragher also highlighted Alexander-Arnold's position in Real's pecking order.

"At the moment, he's actually third-choice right-back for Real Madrid. They're playing a midfield player [Federico Valverde] at right-back, so even in El Clasico, Denzel Dumfries, the first-choice right-back, comes on as a substitute.

"So when you're third choice at a club, they're obviously wanting you to move on."

For now, Alexander-Arnold will be hoping for more minutes in their next three games, two league and one Champions League, before the international break.

He will also be hoping to retain his place in Thomas Tuchel's next England squad, which is due to be announced on 6 November before the Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain.

Alexander-Arnold was recalled for September's international window, ending an absence from the squad dating back to June 2025.

However, with competition for the right-back position remaining strong, his lack of regular playing time at club level could count against him.

Tuchel will therefore have a decision to make over whether to stick with Alexander-Arnold or turn to alternative options.

articles.title: El terremoto Mbappé en China y el precio de una broma: "Una declaración puede arrastrar el valor de socios estratégicos"
articles.standfirst: Varios expertos analizan en MARCA las consecuencias comerciales y reputacionales de la polémica del francés, que ha provocado la ruptura de patrocinios y ha salpicado al Real Madrid, a LaLiga y al resto de clubes
articles.summary: Varios expertos analizan en MARCA las consecuencias comerciales y reputacionales de la polémica del francés, que ha provocado la ruptura de patrocinios y ha salpicado al Real Madrid, a LaLiga y al resto de clubes
articles.body: Tres patrocinadores perdidos, un apagón televisivo y una crisis que ha cruzado fronteras hasta alcanzar los despachos del Real Madrid y de LaLiga. La que se ha liado con Kylian Mbappé ha sobrepasado algunos límites. El crack galo ha comprobado que, en el fútbol de los grandes negocios, una broma puede salir mucho más cara que un error sobre el césped. Un comentario sobre Mao Zedong durante una entrevista distendida desató una tormenta en China, uno de los mercados más codiciados de la industria deportiva. El francés pidió disculpas, pero el daño comercial ya estaba hecho. Lo que comenzó como una anécdota en el programa The Bridge, donde Mbappé recordó un meme que comparaba su figura con la del dirigente chino, terminó convertido en un problema de reputación internacional. ¿Cómo puede una frase de unos segundos poner en riesgo un negocio construido durante años? Un puñado de reputados especialistas en comunicación, marketing y negocio deportivo analizan en MARCA las consecuencias de un episodio que ha evidenciado la fragilidad de las grandes marcas personales. "Futbolistas de élite como Kylian Mbappé son en sí mismos compañías y directivos", explica Juanfer Calderín, CEO de The Queen. Para el especialista, el francés funciona como una multinacional cuyos movimientos afectan a patrocinadores e instituciones. "Un comentario imprudente puede desplomar el valor de las acciones de empresas completas o arrastrar el valor de mercado de socios estratégicos", advierte. Javier Salútregui, CMO de BEYUP by GeoQ, comparte el diagnóstico y señala que muchos deportistas desconocen el alcance de sus identidades de marca compartidas: "Son zonas híbridas de cobranding donde lo personal es público y afecta a toda la cadena de valor de las marcas asociadas". En ese escenario, China constituye un mercado especialmente sensible. Calderín recuerda que el Gobierno de Pekín y sus 1.400 millones de consumidores tienen un peso decisivo para cualquier multinacional. "Una declaración que cuestione su narrativa nacional no se responde con una llamada de atención, sino con la exclusión inmediata del mercado", sostiene. Sin embargo, Ángel Luis Fernández, experto en marketing y patrocinios, introduce un matiz importante: no todas las crisis reputacionales tienen el mismo alcance. "Hay que diferenciar entre una crisis global, provocada por un comportamiento personal que genera rechazo generalizado, y otra que afecta a un mercado concreto por razones culturales o políticas", explica. A su juicio, el caso de Mbappé responde más a una cuestión de intereses económicos que a un deterioro irreversible de su imagen. "Un deportista podría incluso reforzar su figura pública defendiendo determinados valores, pero el problema aparece cuando prácticamente todos sus patrocinadores tienen intereses en un mercado tan grande como el chino". Y concluye: "Muchas decisiones no responden tanto a una cuestión de principios como a la necesidad de proteger el negocio. Es más una crisis de mercado que una verdadera crisis reputacional". La repercusión trasciende al futbolista. El Real Madrid, con una masa de aficionados que Calderín estima cercana a los 100 millones en China, también queda expuesto a una crisis que no ha provocado directamente. Salútregui subraya la excepcionalidad del episodio: "No es la primera vez que vemos errores de branding deportivo, pero sí una de las primeras con una complejidad que va más allá de lo deportivo o comercial. Hablamos de geopolítica". Y sentencia: "El impacto de un meme es directamente proporcional a la fuerza de las marcas a las que se representa. Y el Real Madrid no es una marca cualquiera". David Martín, responsable de Brand España en MARCO, considera que resulta imposible separar completamente al futbolista de su club. "Mbappé ya no es solo un delantero extraordinario; es una multinacional unipersonal. Para el mercado exterior, el jugador porta el escudo las 24 horas del día", señala. El especialista identifica además una carencia en el entorno de algunas superestrellas: la falta de una formación geopolítica y cultural adecuada. La suspensión de las emisiones por parte de CCTV extendió las consecuencias a toda la competición. "El eslabón más vulnerable del ecosistema ha sido, paradójicamente, el que menos control tenía sobre el micrófono: LaLiga", apunta Martín. Marc Menchén, fundador y director de 2Playbook, va un paso más allá y pone el foco en los clubes. El bloqueo televisivo puede perjudicar los ingresos publicitarios de aquellos que se enfrentan al Real Madrid, especialmente por los anuncios de las vallas perimetrales destinados al mercado internacional. "No es solo que haya tenido consecuencias para él directamente, sino que afecta a su club y, en el caso de LaLiga, de forma muy clara al resto de equipos", explica. Una polémica individual amenaza así un negocio del que participan entidades completamente ajenas al incidente. LaLiga respondió con disculpas institucionales y anunció medidas de sensibilización cultural. Para Martín, el episodio refleja una contradicción de la industria: "Consumimos entretenimiento sin fronteras, pero operamos bajo sensibilidades políticas y culturales radicalmente locales". La controversia abre otro debate: ¿pueden los grandes deportistas seguir siendo naturales cuando cualquier palabra amenaza sus contratos? Chema Lamirán, CEO en Digital Media Sports e investigador universitario, encuentra ahí una de las grandes paradojas del negocio. Las marcas necesitan figuras auténticas y cercanas, pero también protegerse de comportamientos que comprometan sus intereses. "En una sociedad hiperconectada, un simple comentario informal puede desatar una crisis de reputación mundial en cuestión de segundos", advierte a este medio. El problema se agrava cuando los mensajes cruzan fronteras. Una broma aceptada en un determinado contexto puede interpretarse como una ofensa en otro. "Ser excesivamente espontáneo implica el riesgo de utilizar códigos humorísticos o culturales locales que resultan ofensivos en otras latitudes", añade Lamirán. Menchén introduce el conflicto entre libertad de expresión y responsabilidad empresarial. Los deportistas, sostiene, deben empezar a medir sus manifestaciones con el mismo cuidado que tradicionalmente han empleado los grandes directivos. Aunque conocen su potencial como plataformas de marketing, quizá no habían asumido hasta ahora que una conversación informal pudiera traducirse inmediatamente en contratos perdidos o bloqueos televisivos. La consecuencia es una comunicación cada vez más calculada, donde la prudencia amenaza con sustituir a la naturalidad. Cuanto mayor es el valor comercial de una estrella, menos margen parece tener para mostrarse tal y como es. Más allá de las consecuencias económicas y reputacionales, la polémica también puede tener un impacto psicológico. Así lo explica Lorena Cos, psicóloga deportiva, quien advierte de que una crisis de esta magnitud puede generar estrés, sensación de pérdida de control y una presión añadida por compensar lo ocurrido a través del rendimiento deportivo. "La preocupación puede interferir en el descanso y la concentración. Estar acostumbrado a la exposición mediática no significa ser inmune a ella", señala. Sin embargo, la especialista pide prudencia a la hora de valorar el estado emocional del francés: "Desconocemos cómo lo está viviendo Mbappé. El impacto dependerá de cómo interprete la situación, de sus recursos para afrontarla y del apoyo de su entorno". Mbappé pidió disculpas en varios idiomas, pero las consecuencias económicas ya habían demostrado que el episodio superaba una simple polémica en redes sociales. Calderín recuerda que Estados Unidos, Oriente Medio y el Sudeste Asiático también representan territorios estratégicos donde cualquier declaración puede tener implicaciones comerciales. "La era del deportista que solo habla en el campo terminó hace años", sentencia Martín. Menchén recurre a una conocida máxima de Spiderman para resumir las nuevas obligaciones de las estrellas: "Un gran poder conlleva una gran responsabilidad". Su influencia digital les proporciona enormes oportunidades, pero también compromisos con los clubes y empresas que sostienen su negocio. Lamirán cierra con una reflexión sobre el precio de esa exposición: "El éxito internacional te exige convertirte en un espejo en el que todas las culturas quieran mirarse; la gran incógnita es qué sucede cuando, al mirarte tú mismo, ya no eres capaz de reconocerte". El episodio del crack madridista con China ha dejado una lección para toda la industria: construir una marca global exige años de trabajo; poner en peligro parte de su valor puede ser cuestión de segundos.

articles.title: Lamine Yamal, Raphinha help Barcelona hammer Alaves to retain Liga top spot
articles.summary: Yamal and Raphinha score two goals each as Barcelona recover from last week’s loss in El Clasico to move back on top.
articles.body:
Raphinha and Lamine Yamal have each struck twice as Barcelona have thrashed Alaves 6-1 to reclaim their La Liga lead and get back on track after two damaging defeats in the past week.

Earlier, Atletico Madrid, in second, earned a solid 2-0 win at Levante, but Barca moved two points clear of the Rojiblancos by routing the Basque visitors at Camp Nou on Saturday.

Still stinging after a Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain and then last weekend’s La Liga home El Clasico loss against rivals Real Madrid, Hansi Flick’s side found their groove once more on Saturday.

Raphinha netted twice in the first half on either side of a Fermin Lopez strike, and Yamal found the net just before the interval.

The teenage winger netted again midway through the second half, and substitute Anthony Gordon chipped home Barca’s sixth before Mariano Diaz pulled one back for Alaves.

“It was a hard week for us. There was no better place than Camp Nou in front of our fans [to bounce back],” Lopez told Movistar.

“They make the difference, Lamine and Raphinha. With them, we will achieve big things.”

There was a minute of silence at the start of each of the day’s matches in memory of the 69 people killed on Wednesday in a train crash in the province of Toledo.

Barcelona host Aston Villa in the Champions League on Tuesday and travel to face Atletico next Sunday in a table-topping La Liga clash.

Alaves have now gone seven matches without a win but are 10th.

“We have to turn the page quickly,” midfielder Ander Guevara said. “We don’t need to sound the alarms. We know we’re on a bad run, but we’re a mature and humble team.”

Earlier in Valencia, Diego Simeone’s Atletico had temporarily climbed a point clear of the Catalan giants with goals from Alejandro Grimaldo and Giuliano Simeone against Levante.

Atletico recorded a seventh consecutive league win to continue their strong form and put pressure on the reigning champions.

“I’m very happy with the team’s work,” coach Simeone told Movistar.

“We’re very far from the end of the season. … We’ll keep going game by game.”

Alex Baena, the visitors’ main creative outlet, set up both goals as Diego Simeone recorded his 344th La Liga win at the helm of Atletico, matching the club’s record set by Luis Aragones.

“I don’t feel it much as mine, but it belongs to my players, everyone who has been with me for so many years,” said Simeone, who started coaching Atletico in 2011.

Among Sunday’s fixtures, Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid, in third, will visit Racing Santander.

articles.title: Hansi Flick, un técnico de récords
articles.standfirst: Ya suma 100 victorias con el Barcelona
articles.summary: Ya suma 100 victorias con el Barcelona
articles.body: El Barcelona recuperó, con su triunfo ayer sábado contra el Alavés, mucho más que el liderato y la confianza tras las derrotas contra el PSG y el Real Madrid. Dio un golpe sobre la mesa para confirmar que no regalará el primer puesto de la tabla y reiteró la calidad de un vestuario en el que no sólo logran récords sus estrellas, como Raphinha o Lamine Yamal que se están acostumbrado a pulverizar registros. Hansi Flick también está haciendo historia. El técnico alemán firmó contra el Alavés, en el encuentro de ayer sábado disputado en el Spotify Camp Nou, su victoria número 100 en el banquillo del Barcelona. Y lo ha logrado en un tiempo récord que le permite convertirse en leyenda del equipo culé: los cien triunfos de Hansi Flick han llegado en tan solo 131 partidos, una estadística que lo sitúa como el segundo mejor de toda la historia del Barça. Únicamente le supera Luis Enrique, que alcanzó esa cifra de éxitos en 126 compromisos. Consiguió 44 victorias en las temporadas 24-25 y 25-26 y ya ha firmado 12 en la presente, la 26-27. En 14 partidos. En estos 100 cruces, ha evidenciado, además, su apuesta por el fútbol ofensivo: el Barça ha marcado 375 goles y ha encajado 153. Pero, además, el preparador germano ha logrado la gesta firmando un 76,33% de victorias, cifras que le sitúan como el entrenador de la historia del Barcelona con un mejor porcentaje de victorias, cogiendo como referencia el total de partidos del resto de técnicos y no solo sus 100 primeros. Flick, que ha ganado cinco títulos en las dos temporadas completas que lleva al frente del Barça, no es muy partidario ni de detenerse en sí mismo ni en mirar hacia atrás, pero tiene claro qué triunfo destaca de todos estos cien. "Teníamos las esperanza de dirigir 100 partidos con el Barcelona y ahora son 100 ganados. Si tuviera que quedarme con un éxito tal vez sería la primera victoria en el Clásico, en Madrid... Ese triunfo me trae buenos recuerdos", dijo ayer el preparador alemán, sabedor de la importancia para los culés de doblegar al eterno rival. Flick es uno de los grandes motivos de orgullo de Joan Laporta, que hace unos meses, a mediados de mayo, renovó su contrato hasta junio de 2028 con opción a otro curso más.

articles.title: Why Lionel Messi isn't suspended after five yellow cards this season: The MLS rule that doesn't exist in other leagues
articles.summary: Discover how MLS's unique Good Behaviour Incentive allows Lionel Messi to avoid suspension despite receiving five yellow cards this season. Understand the rules that keep him eligible for crucial matches with Inter Miami.
articles.body: Five yellow cards would normally leave Lionel Messi facing a one-match suspension in any other league, but the Inter Miami captain will be available for Sunday's meeting with New England Revolution. His reprieve comes through one of Major League Soccer's less familiar regulations, which allows players to have cautions removed from their disciplinary record after a sustained run of good behaviour.What is the MLS Good Behaviour Incentive?Messi picked up his fifth yellow card of the 2026 MLS season during Inter Miami’s 2-2 draw with FC Cincinnati on Wednesday, October 28. The booking came in the 44th minute, after the Argentine approached referee Armando Villarreal following a collision involving Cincinnati defender Samuel Gidi. Under MLS’s regular-season disciplinary rules, five yellow cards ordinarily bring a $250 fine and an automatic one-match suspension, which would have ruled Messi out of Sunday's meeting with New England Revolution.However, the league's Good Behaviour Incentive allows a player to remove one caution from his accumulated total for every five consecutive appearances without receiving a yellow card, red card or supplemental disciplinary sanction. Messi has completed two such qualifying runs this season, reducing his active tally from five bookings to three and keeping him available for Inter Miami's next match.The provision appears in the league's official Competition Guidelines:“A player will automatically reduce his yellow card accumulation total by one yellow card each time he appears in five consecutive matches without receiving a yellow card, red card or supplemental discipline in such matches.“For clarity, a player cannot have a negative yellow card accumulation total; the Good Behavior Incentive can only reset to a zero-card total. This incentive will be automatically applied a maximum of three times throughout the course of the MLS Regular Season.”The reduction takes effect once the fifth qualifying match has been completed. A player can benefit from it a maximum of three times during the regular season, although the accumulation cannot fall below zero.How Messi's five yellow cards became threeMessi's disciplinary record during the 2026 MLS regular season shows how the incentive has kept him below the suspension threshold. He has received five bookings, but two separate runs of five consecutive matches without disciplinary action reduced his accumulated total by one caution each time.His bookings and the subsequent reductions unfolded as follows:April 12, 2026 – Colorado Rapids (Matchday 8): Messi received his first yellow card of the season.May 3, 2026 – Orlando City (Matchday 11): He was booked again, taking his accumulation to two.After Orlando City: Messi completed five consecutive matches without a yellow card, red card or supplemental discipline. The first Good Behaviour reduction removed one caution, bringing his total down to one.June 21, 2026 – Nashville SC (Matchday 20): Messi received another booking, taking his accumulation to two.After Nashville: He then completed 10 consecutive matches without another booking or disciplinary sanction. That run triggered the incentive twice, removing two cautions from his accumulation and bringing the total back down to zero.September 13, 2026 – Atlanta United (Matchday 31): Messi was booked again, taking his active accumulation to one.October 29, 2026 – FC Cincinnati (Matchday 33): He received his fifth yellow card of the season, this time in the 44th minute for dissent after a collision involving Cincinnati defender Samuel Gidi. His active accumulation rose to three.The two reductions explain why Messi's latest booking did not take him to the five-card suspension threshold. Although he has been cautioned five times during the campaign, his official accumulation stands at three.Why Messi's availability matters for Inter MiamiMessi's reprieve comes ahead of Inter Miami's meeting with New England Revolution on Sunday, with the two sides separated by just two points. The result could have a significant bearing on the Eastern Conference standings, as a victory for Kily Gonzalez's side would take Inter Miami above its opponents and into second place with one game remaining.The clubs last met on April 26, 2026, when they played out a 1-1 draw at Inter Miami's home ground. Carles Gil and Germán Berterame scored in that encounter, leaving Sunday's fixture with an opportunity for either side to gain an advantage in the closing stages of the regular season.A higher finish would also bring better seeding for the MLS Cup, a competition Messi will be hoping to lead Inter Miami to win for the second time. The Argentine has been central to the club's campaign, scoring 25 goals in 29 appearances and leading the league's scoring charts as he pursues the Golden Boot.Had the Good Behaviour Incentive not reduced his accumulation, Messi's fifth booking against Cincinnati would have left him facing a suspension. Instead, he is available for a fixture that could determine where Inter Miami finishes in the Eastern Conference.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Dave Challinor: Sheffield Wednesday appoint former Stockport County boss
articles.summary: Sheffield Wednesday appoint former Stockport County boss Dave Challinor as their new manager.
articles.body:
Sheffield Wednesday have appointed former Stockport County boss Dave Challinor as their new manager.

He replaces Henrik Pedersen, who was sacked last Sunday after just one win in six League One games.

The Owls are currently on a winless run of three matches - where they have drawn once and lost twice - and are ninth in the table.

They next play Blackpool at 14:00 GMT on Sunday, for which Challinor will be watching from the stands as interim boss Matt Hamshaw takes charge.

A former Bury and Tranmere Rovers defender, Challinor began his managerial career at Colwyn Bay in 2010.

The 51-year-old has since achieved multiple promotions across spells with AFC Fylde and Hartlepool.

More recently, he guided Stockport County from the National League and to the League Two title within three seasons - and twice took them to the League One play-offs.

The Englishman departed the Hatters by mutual consent at the conclusion of the 2025-26 season after losing in the play-off final to Bolton Wanderers.

Sheffield Wednesday's new owners wanted to bring in a winner - someone capable of turning recent defeats and draws into victories.

Challinor's record fits the bill, with seven promotions to his name already. He also knows League One through his time at Stockport County.

His task will be to provide an effective form of football. He has to bring a Sheffield Wednesday squad together that has talented individuals but now needs to be shaped into a team.

The top seven in League One is starting to look strong and Wednesday, along with Leicester and possibly the rising MK Dons, will be looking at joining the group that appears to be establishing.

This will be an interesting next step for Challinor. It's a very different job to Stockport, Hartlepool or Fylde - with massive expectations.

Whenever Wednesday are in League One, you're expected to win. A lot. Darren Moore had a 96-point season at this level and was always only a bad result away from having people question his job.

I'd expect he will probably be joined by Clint Hill and Anthony Sweeney on his staff. Simon Wilson, who worked with Challinor at Stockport, will have been instrumental in the appointment. That working relationship will be key moving forward.

articles.title: Simón y Oyarzabal, una historia de amigos
articles.standfirst: Portero del Athletic y delantero de la Real mantienen una relación especial desde que coincidieron en categorías inferiores
articles.summary: Portero del Athletic y delantero de la Real mantienen una relación especial desde que coincidieron en categorías inferiores
articles.body: Unai Simón y Mikel Oyarzabal son campeones del mundo y cosecha del 97. Al tiempo que dos abanderados de Athletic y Real Sociedad. Este domingo se cruzarán en un derbi especial en San Mamés por eso de ser el primero después de que Simón recogiese el lunes el título a mejor portero del mundo. También porque en la previa del partido, 50 años después de que ocurriera en el viejo Atotxa, Iribar y Kortabarria, entonces capitanes de Athletic y Real, portarán la ikurriña que lucieron en 1976 casi de manera clandestina. Simón y Oyarzabal serían dignos sucesores de aquella imagen recogiendo ese legado del que tan profundo y bien habló Simón en la gala del Balón de Oro. En el entremés de este derbi el discurso de Simón fue comentado por las dos aficiones y los dos vestuarios. Y contaban en San Sebastián que bien podría haberlo firmado Oyarzabal, con el que mantiene una conexión especial. Nunca han defendido la misma camiseta en un club, pero sí han compartido distintas categorías con Euskadi y España, con la que además han brillado en los últimos campeonatos de manera individual. El portero, de Murgia, y el delantero, de Eibar, conectaron pronto. Desde las primeras veces que se vieron con Euskadi supieron que tenían mucho en común. Comparten muchos rasgos del carácter, también la pasión por el equipo al que pertenecen y la responsabilidad de entender que para muchos niños son referencia. Los dos tienen refugios en sus amigos de toda la vida y no acostumbran a vivir de la ostentación. También se manifiestan con extrema calidez cuando la ocasión lo demanda. “Te quiero Unai Simón”, escribió Oyarzabal en RRSS cuando el portero fue clave en la tanda de penaltis que clasificó a España para las semifinales de la Eurocopa 2021. Ese verano los dos fueron uña y carne con una selección a la que después volvieron como ganadores. Ese verano llegó después de una final de Copa entre Athletic y Real que ganaron los txuriurdin con un gol de penalti...marcado por Oyarzabal. Portero y delantero estuvieron más enfrente que nunca, pero conscientes de que lo que ocurriera con aquel lanzamiento no les iba a distanciar más que en el resultado del partido. Semanas después, cuando se incorporaron a la concentración de la Eurocopa, viajaron en el mismo avión de línea regular hasta Madrid y desde el aeropuerto a Las Rozas lo hicieron compartiendo confidencias en el mismo taxi. No son divos. Son amigos y futbolistas. Dignos capitanes de Athletic y Real.

articles.title: Lizarazu señala dónde se le escapó a Mbappé el Balón de Oro: "Perdió el control completamente"
articles.standfirst: El exinternacional francés analiza la campaña del madridista por el galardón
articles.summary: El exinternacional francés analiza la campaña del madridista por el galardón
articles.body: El Balón de Oro sigue coleando en Francia. El país que lo entrega vio cómo su máxima estrella se quedaba a 28 puntos de conseguir el galardón, a 28 puntos de un Harry Kane que fue el gran triunfador de la noche. Bixente Lizarazu, analista en Telefoot, analizó ese segundo puesto de Mbappé y apuntó dónde pudo perder ese puñado de votos que le faltó para ganar el Balón de Oro: "Nos brindó un gran Mundial; me pareció que fue un capitán coherente de la selección francesa, con un mensaje de equipo contundente. Pero luego, con el incidente del Balón de Oro, perdió completamente el control. No me gustó nada". "Se desvió hacia una postura hiperindividualista, carente de humildad, centrándose en la autopromoción y olvidándose en cierto modo de los demás. Daba la impresión de que él era el único que importaba y que nadie más existía. ¿Le perjudicó eso? No lo creo, porque, en última instancia, fueron 100 periodistas de 100 países quienes tomaron la decisión", amplió Lizarazu. El exinternacional galo espera que en el próximo parón internacional Mbappé esté centrado y abandone una actitud individualista: "Ahora necesita volver a la selección francesa centrándose en el trabajo en equipo. Porque, pase lo que pase, son esos valores de equipo los que harán ganar a Francia. Y viene de una etapa en la que no ha ganado ni con sus clubes ni con sus selecciones nacionales". Y le dejó una última reflexión para el futuro: "Puede que marque muchos goles, pero necesita ayudar a su equipo a ganar. Eso es lo más importante".

articles.title: Mass Shooting After Alabama Football Game Leaves 1 Dead, 8 Wounded
articles.summary: BIRMINGHAM, Ala. (AP) — One person was killed and eight others were wounded in a mass shooting just outside Legion Field after the annual 'Magic City Classic' football game on Saturday night, police in Birmingham, Ala., said.
articles.body:
BIRMINGHAM, Ala. (AP) — One person was killed and eight others were wounded in a mass shooting just outside Legion Field after the annual 'Magic City Classic' football game on Saturday night, police in Birmingham, Ala., said.

Michael Pickett, chief of the Birmingham Police Department, said most spectators and families had left the stadium property after the game, but the shooting happened nearby, where vendors were set up along Graymont Avenue.

He said he was "very grateful that more people weren't injured."

The circumstances of the shooting were unclear.

Police spokesperson De'Rell Freeman said one person had been detained and transported to police headquarters for questioning, and "multiple weapons" had been found and secured.

articles.title: Luis García Plaza repite alineación por primera vez esta temporada
articles.standfirst: Ante el Getafe, el Sevilla mantiene los mismos once jugadores que vencieron a Osasuna
articles.summary: Ante el Getafe, el Sevilla mantiene los mismos once jugadores que vencieron a Osasuna
articles.body: El Sevilla asienta poco a poco su once tipo. De cara al partido de este domingo frente al Getafe, Luis García Plaza ha decidido darle continuidad al equipo que ya doblegó en casa a Osasuna por 2-0 en la última jornada liguera. Además de mantener a la misma defensa y a Chidera Ejuke por la banda derecha, el entrenador madrileño apuesta de nuevo por un doble pivote conformado por Lucien Agoumé y Youssouf Fofana para escoltar a los dos delanteros, en este caso Isaac Romero y Lucas Stassin, titulares por cuarta vez en lo que va de curso. Por lo tanto, el Sevilla saltará al césped del Coliseum con un 4-2-3-1 compuesto por Odysseas; Juan Iglesias, Castrín, Kike Salas, Suazo; Agoumé, Fofana; Ejuke, Isaac Romero, Félix Correia; y Lucas Stassin. Es la primera vez que Luis García Plaza repite la misma alineación en dos jornadas consecutivas durante la presente temporada, la tercera desde que está al frente del banquillo hispalense, pues la pasada campaña ya lo hizo primero contra Atlético de Madrid y Levante y luego contra Real Sociedad y Espanyol. El once titular que presenta el Sevilla ante el Getafe es también muy parecido al que se ya impuso al Valencia en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán (1-0). Aquel día, el conjunto blanquirrojo partió de inicio con los mismos futbolistas a excepción de Miguel Sierra, baja de larga duración por una lesión en el hombro y única ausencia junto con Marcao. Hasta el momento, parece que Chidera Ejuke es el que está ganando la pelea por relevar en la derecha al extremo granadino.

articles.title: 'Not Acceptable' - Regis Le Bris Demands Sunderland Change After Coventry Defeat
articles.summary: Sunderland boss Regis Le Bris has demanded improvements from his side after the 3-1 defeat at Coventry City on Saturday.
articles.body:
Regis Le Bris' Sunderland side were shocking in the 3-1 defeat at Coventry City

Sunderland have now made seven individual errors directly leading to goals conceded this season following the Coventry City defeat, and Regis Le Bris has demanded change as a result.

Sunderland were battered 3-1 by Coventry on Saturday, seeing Frank Lampard's side come out best in every department after goals from Tatsuhiro Sakamoto, Taiwo Awoniyi and Jack Rudoni, with Enzo Le Fee netting an inconsequential penalty which failed to inspire a face-saving comeback.

On a scary Halloween performance from Sunderland , the Black Cats ironically dug their own graves on the spooky afternoon, with the Black Cats yet again making grave errors in defence.

It is one of many extremely worrying aspects of Sunderland's play this season, and one which Le Bris must solve rapidly, as in his words, it will see the opponent "kill you," as Coventry emphatically did.

Regis Le Bris Demands Sunderland Stop 'Unacceptable' Issue

For Coventry's opening goal, Trai Hume's failed attempted clearance unfortunately ricocheted of teammate Luke O'Nien to see the ball kindly to the feet of Sakamoto, with the Japanese international curling a stellar low strike past Robin Roefs to break the deadlock after just 16 minutes and set the Sky Blues on course for a comfortable win.

Just twenty minutes later, with Sunderland showing no signs of improvement, the Black Cats once again caused their own downfall in defence to allow Awoniyi far too much space and freedom for the second.

Chris Rigg's ball into O'Nien saw the Sunderland defender dispossessed before Coventry frontman Awoniyi broke through and burst through several last failed tackle attempts from the recovering Black Cats defence to fire past Roefs and double his side's advantage.

Far too often this season, Sunderland have collectively dug their own graves in defence with costly individual errors, and Le Bris is desperate to extinguish this element of the rock-bottom Black Cats' current state going forward.

Le Bris told Sunderland's media after Coventry: "We gave two opportunities from two unforced errors.

"But this inconsistency is not acceptable at all. Consistency is the key word in this league. If you keep making individual mistakes, the opponent will kill you.

"We won't give up. We're trying to find solutions."

Another worrying element of Sunderland's defensive play is the increased ill-discipline in Le Bris' side, with the Black Cats now having the highest amount of red cards (three) so far this season within the Premier League after the once-again shocking Omar Alderete was given his marching orders in injury time by referee Simon Hooper.

However, red cards can be put down to game state and the fact that every team in the Premier League will pick up a red at points throughout the campaign.

But crucially, no Premier League side makes as many individual errors in defence as Sunderland have done (seven) so far this season, and these costly mistakes could cost Le Bris his job at the Stadium of Light if they are not stamped out, and soon.
