articles.title: Ismael Saibari undergoes surgery for ligament tear as Bayern injury timelines surface
articles.summary: FC Bayern have now confirmed that both Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry will be sidelined with injury for the foreseeable future.In a press release issued by...
articles.body:
FC Bayern have now confirmed that both Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry will be sidelined with injury for the foreseeable future.

In a press release issued by the club, it was noted that both had sustained their respective injury issues during Saturday evening's Bundesliga clash with Borussia Dortmund.

The Bavarian giants maintained their place at the top of the pile with a 2-2 draw at the Allianz Arena .

Bayern set to be without Ismael Saibari and Serge Gnabry

A game that promised to put Bayern three points clear of their arch rivals early on in the Bundesliga title race.

Yet, one that ended in a share of the spoils – and at great cost for Aaron Danks' men, with Michael Olise asking to be substituted in the second half of action.

Saibari is understood to have suffered a tear to the syndesmotic ligament in his right ankle and has already undergone successful surgery to address the issue.

Gnabry, on the other hand, picked up a muscle injury in his left hamstring. Both issues will likely see the attacking duo sitting in the treatment room for several weeks and months.

Bayern Munich may have to dip into the January market

It's not looking fantastic for Bayern's offensive options at present:

Luis Diaz: Torn muscle bundle (out until late November)

Ismael Saibari: Syndesmotic ligament tear (out until start of February at the earliest)

Serge Gnabry: Hamstring injury (out until December)

Jamal Musiala is expected to be back in the squad in the near future. However, reporting around the club indicates we'll be without the Germany international for Tuesday's Champions League clash against Atletico Madrid in the Spanish capital.

Theoretically, if all goes to plan with recovery schedules, Bayern will have a full complement of attacking talent available come January.

But the question remains: should the recruitment team look to take precautionary action to boost chances of a successful campaign in the knockout stages of the Champions League? Bayern Munich would happily add the right man to the ranks to provide cover for Luis Diaz on the left flank, but it remains to be seen whether the right profile emerges on the market for the money Bayern are comfortable paying.

And history already tells us – as Jan-Christian Dreesen was keen to remind us all this week – that January transfers are a no-go in Munich unless the perfect conditions arise.

articles.title: Matos' Swansea like Klopp's Liverpool - Mowbray
articles.summary: Blackburn Rovers boss Tony Mowbray says Swansea City's intensity under Vitor Matos reminds him of Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool.
articles.body:
Blackburn Rovers boss Tony Mowbray says Swansea City under Vitor Matos remind him of Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool.

Swansea turned on the style as they bounced back to form by beating Blackburn 4-0 on Saturday.

Rovers had arrived at the Swansea.com Stadium in good form, but were overwhelmed as Matos' team registered their biggest victory of the season.

Mowbray said Swansea's triumph was built on their "amazingly good" intensity – and that brought back memories of Klopp's Liverpool.

Matos, who took charge of the Swans last November, spent five years on Klopp's Anfield staff.

"My previous Blackburn team, particularly through Covid, played Liverpool quite a little bit," Mowbray said.

"We weren't in the Premier League but we played Liverpool in Covid just to get their team up to speed, we played them twice I think at Anfield and once at Ewood Park.

"Liverpool of those days were absolutely amazing because they didn't let you breathe, and you can see bits of that with this [Swansea] team. There seemed to be three men closing every one of our players down."

Swansea's triumph means they are second in the Championship, with 26 points banked from their first 13 games of the season.

The vastly experienced Mowbray, 62, reckons Swansea look like a team capable of contending for promotion this season – although he warned that their tactical approach will not always bring rewards.

"I think when you play against the best teams, the coaches will know that you're number one at high pressing, know you're going to swarm all over the ball and the pitch," he said of Swansea's game plan.

"[They will] just not take risks, just turn you around and let you swarm over nothing because there's nobody trying to pass it out from the back.

"They'll be kicking every goal-kick long. They'll be playing a big centre-forward and trying to get two little fast guys running in behind."

He added: "It's great coaching, it's great philosophy, but I'm saying there are coaches in this league who'll be watching.

"We're only 13 games in, [Matos] has got a lot of football still to play and there'll be a lot of teams where they won't be able to [do that] because there'll be nothing to press."

Stephen Eustaquio, Joseph Opoku and Filip Lissah struck to put Swansea 3-0 up at half-time before Ross Stewart's fine second-half goal condemned Blackburn to their heaviest defeat since April 2024.

Mowbray's frustration was that his team failed to adapt to Swansea's approach despite working on a game plan last week.

"If you'd have seen some of our football this year, it's been pretty good, but against that intensity, we really struggled," he said.

"We shouldn't be playing around the edges of our box and giving a team who are number one pressing in the league the chance to do what they're really good at."

articles.title: Lincoln Riley situation at USC is more difficult after win | Opinion
articles.summary: We don't duck the tough questions around here, so we are going to confront the Lincoln Riley situation at USC after the victory over Ohio State:
articles.body:
Lincoln Riley had his back against the wall Saturday night. The embattled USC football coach faced an Ohio State team without its starting quarterback, at home and in the primetime television slot on NBC. This was a must-win for a man who has largely failed to do his job in nearly five full seasons in Los Angeles. Most USC fans wanted him gone entering this game. How much does this win change Riley's outlook? We're going to tell it straight, because that's what we always aim to do. We're not going to sell you false hope, but we're also going to offer our own view of what USC should do. Let's go:

We have discussed in recent weeks what athletic director Jennifer Cohen would and should do at USC in light of Lincoln Riley's struggles. Let's be brutally honest here: This win over Ohio State will very probably make Cohen keep Riley for 2027. It's not what fans want to hear, but again, giving people an accurate read of what's going on is what we should strive to do, instead of selling false hope. I personally would not retain Riley just yet, but it's likely that Riley will stay for a sixth season as USC coach due to this win over a big-name program. If we had to guess, Cohen is not going to abandon Riley after the coach took down the Big Ten's most annually successful program (not in a three-year window, but over the course of the past 60 years of college football).

We just told you where we think Jennifer Cohen stands on Lincoln Riley. Our own view is that Riley and USC need to go into Indiana and beat Curt Cignetti in two weeks to earn retention for 2027. It's just not enough to beat an Ohio State team playing without its starting quarterback at home. Beating Indiana on the road and taking down Curt Cignetti, the best coach in college football, would be a truly resounding statement about the condition of the USC program. A signature road win, something Riley hasn't achieved at any point in his tenure in Los Angeles, would be significant enough to warrant attention. Unless or until he gets the job done, we personally don't think Riley should be retained for next season... but again, we aren't making the decisions here. Jen Cohen is.

Lincoln Riley released a statement after the Ohio State game saying how much he wants to be the USC head coach. Given how much he is being paid, why wouldn't he? That point aside, we don't think Riley wants to admit defeat. He wants to figure this thing out in LA and get USC over the hump. He won't leave for Baylor or a Big 12 job. He wants to stay, in our view.

The win over Ohio State makes it really hard from a negotiating standpoint to convince Riley and his representation that accepting a lower buyout figure is palatable. A loss to the Buckeyes might have boxed Riley into a corner and given USC and Cohen more leverage. Now? It's a lot more difficult to get Riley to meet USC halfway on this sticky issue. No one wants to pay a full $70 million buyout. That's part of why this Ohio State result does feel significant in terms of determining Riley's status at USC going into 2027.

The argument Lincoln Riley always had for staying at USC in 2027 was that "I just need one more recruiting cycle with Chad Bowden" to stockpile talent and depth in the program and reach the point where the roster is truly built to contend for championships. Beating Ohio State gives Riley the ability to say "We're almost there and now we just need to finish the job next year." Lincoln Riley can say that one more year of Trent Mosley and Luke Wafle and Jahkeem Stewart and Kayden Dixon-Wyatt, combined with incoming recruits, might put USC over the top.

We don't agree with Riley, but again, the political weight of this Ohio State win will make Riley's position and overall sales pitch more convincing to the people who matter: the administrators and major donors.

We aren't fully sold on Lincoln Riley, as you know, but with that having been said, the Gary Patterson hire looks better - not worse - as time goes along. This is a more mature and competent defense than what USC had last year. The run defense wasn't great against Ohio State, but when you consider how badly the Trojans were gashed by Illinois and Notre Dame, this is so much better by comparison. USC is able to stand tall in the red zone and doesn't allow 60-yard touchdown gallops. It's a low bar given how badly the 2025 run defense performed, but it's better, and against Ohio State, it mattered. Patterson hasn't oversold this defense but has gradually brought it along. The defense wasn't the reason USC lost at Wisconsin, either. Oregon was awful, but otherwise, this defense has largely done its job. It hasn't been great, but the product is undeniably better than 2025. Credit to Patterson and to Riley for making a hire which has moved the needle in the right direction.

Could Riley be fired if USC loses to Indiana and UCLA?

We haven't yet talked about the Bob Chesney-UCLA factor, so let's do that. If USC loses not only to Cignetti and Indiana, but to Chesney and UCLA, could that get Riley fired? We would certainly hand Riley a pink slip, but would Jen Cohen have the stomach to do that? The chances of this happening, given the win over Ohio State and what it added to Riley's column in terms of the backroom (and buyout) politics, are low. Only if USC gets blown out by both IU and UCLA could Riley still be in trouble. The odds are low. We do have to admit that the optics of UCLA making the College Football Playoff in Year 1 under Bob Chesney, while Lincoln Riley goes 0 for 5, would be terrible. Still, that "give me one more year and one more recruiting class" argument is easier for Riley to sell to Jen Cohen now that he has beaten Ohio State.

Here's the very uncomfortable truth about Lincoln Riley and USC football: Riley might lose to Indiana, then beat a UCLA team playing with a backup quarterback. USC would finish 9-3, just like last year. The Trojans would be bad enough to miss the playoff - making the season a failure - but they would be close enough to the playoff that Riley would be able to say, with some degree of legitimacy, that the program is very close to breaking through. It would be, in many ways, the worst of both worlds: no ultimate prize and no firing of Riley. Fans don't get the playoff and don't get a coaching change. They get neither. 0 for 2.

You can all see it coming. We can too. It would be the least satisfying outcome because it would mean nothing has really changed.

This Ohio State win isn't necessarily a bad thing for USC, but it can't end here. USC and Lincoln Riley have to at least win one of the Indiana or UCLA games for anyone to think real progress has been made, and even then, winning only one of the two means the Trojans miss the playoff for the 13th consecutive year, which is a failure.

If this Ohio State win really is going to mean something, Lincoln Riley needs to beat both Indiana and UCLA, get to 10-2, make the playoff, and truly end the debate about whether he is the right man for this program. Anything less will feel, to us, like failure.

Jen Cohen and USC brass might not see it the same way.

We said we wouldn't duck the tough conversations. That's reality as we see it after the win over Ohio State.

articles.title: One killed, eight others wounded in shooting outside Legion Field following Alabama A&M's win over Alabama State
articles.summary: It's the second straight weekend a mass shooting has taken place following a college football game.
articles.body:
One person was killed and eight others were shot outside of Birmingham's Legion Field after the annual game between Alabama A&M and Alabama State on Saturday night.

Police said they found multiple gunshot victims after arriving to the scene. The shooting happened just before 8 p.m. local time after Alabama A&M beat Alabama State 31-28. A person has been detained and multiple firearms were recovered from the scene.

"Everyone knows this is the largest event we have here in the city and it's extremely taxing on our personnel," Birmingham Police Chief Michael Pickett said in a statement via WBRC. "Other leaders in law enforcement recognize that and they quickly offered up support and we are grateful for that quick response. I'll end with this .. our Birmingham police officers are true heroes. They are true heroes. Seeing the courage and resilience they displayed tonight, running alongside them in the directing of those gunshots, triaging people as we pass by them going in the direction of the shots to make sure they weren't injured, or if they were injured, rendering aid as we continue toward the gunfire. That shows true courage, that shows the true dedication they have to actually saving lives. And I'm thankful that all of our police officers as well others who were of assistance are able to go home to their families tonight.

The incident marks the second straight weekend that a mass shooting has taken place outside a college football game. On Oct. 24, 11 people were shot after a fight broke out after Florida A&M's homecoming game in Tallahassee.

Tallahassee Police Chief Lawrence Revell told people at the Tabernacle Missionary Baptist Church on Thursday that police estimated there were thousands of people on Perry Street outside of Bragg Memorial Stadium following the game.

As of Thursday, six of the 11 wounded in the shooting were still hospitalized

"That fight broke up. There was another fight just shortly after that. And then right after that. But in two minutes, a gun was brought into that scene, handed from one youth to another, and then a number of shots were fired," he said. "We estimate anywhere from 3,000 to 6,000 people were probably on Perry Street. So I thank the Lord Jesus Christ that we had no deaths," he added.
